summary.en: The Western Zhou capital: the twin cities of Feng and Hao on either side of the Feng River, near present-day Xi'an. It was sacked in 771 BCE.
summary.zh: 西周都城，由沣河两岸的丰京和镐京组成，在今西安附近。前771年遭到洗劫。

detail.en: Excavations at the Feng–Hao site have found palace foundations, bronze workshops and cemeteries. The point marks the site area.
detail.zh: 丰镐遗址出土过宫殿基址、铸铜作坊和墓地。图上的点标在遗址区。

summary.en: The eastern Zhou capital in the Luoyang basin, seat of the Zhou kings from the move east until 256 BCE.
summary.zh: 东周都城，在洛阳盆地。从东迁到前256年，周王一直居住在这里。

detail.en: The texts name two cities here, the royal city and Chengzhou, a few kilometres apart. The point marks the Luoyang area.
detail.zh: 史书在这里提到两座城：王城和成周，相距不远。图上的点标在洛阳一带。

summary.en: King You of Zhou is killed below Mount Li by the forces of the Marquis of Shen and the Quanrong; Haojing is sacked.
summary.zh: 周幽王在骊山下被申侯和犬戎的军队杀死，镐京遭到洗劫。

detail.en: The Shiji tells the famous story that the king had lit the alarm beacons to amuse his consort Bao Si, so that no one came when they were lit in earnest. The excavated Xinian has no such story and gives a different sequence of rival kings.
detail.zh: 《史记》记载了一个著名的故事：幽王为博褒姒一笑点燃烽火，等到犬戎真的打来，再点烽火已经没有诸侯来救。出土的《系年》没有这个故事，所记的王位更替次序也不同。

summary.en: Lu's court chronicle, the Spring and Autumn Annals, begins with the first year of Duke Yin of Lu.
summary.zh: 鲁国的编年史《春秋》从鲁隐公元年开始记事。

detail.en: Its entries are terse: deaths of rulers, meetings, attacks, eclipses. Many of the solar eclipses it records can be matched with real ones, which helps to check its dates.
detail.zh: 它的记事非常简短：国君去世、会盟、征伐、日食。书中记录的日食，许多能与真实发生的日食对上，这有助于核对它的年代。

summary.en: Capital of Lu and home of Confucius.
summary.zh: 鲁国都城，孔子的家乡。

detail.en: Lu was founded for a son of the Duke of Zhou, and its court kept the Spring and Autumn Annals. The point marks the modern city.
detail.zh: 鲁国是周公之子的封国，鲁国史官记下了《春秋》。图上的点标在今天的曲阜城。

summary.en: Zheng defeats a royal army led by King Huan of Zhou; an arrow wounds the king.
summary.zh: 郑军击败周桓王亲自率领的王师，周王中箭受伤。

detail.en: According to the Zuo Tradition, the king's troops were joined by those of Chen, Cai and Wey, and Zheng broke the weaker wings first. The Zheng officer Zhu Dan shot the king in the shoulder, but Duke Zhuang refused to pursue him and that night sent a minister to ask after his health. No casualty figures are recorded.
detail.zh: 据《左传》，随王出征的还有陈、蔡、卫三国军队，郑军先击溃较弱的两翼。郑国大夫祝聃射中周王肩膀，郑庄公却不许追击，当夜还派大臣去慰问周王。伤亡人数没有记载。

title.en: Di forces take the Wey capital

summary.en: Di forces defeat Wey at Yingze, kill Duke Yi and take the capital, Chaoge.
summary.zh: 狄人在荧泽击败卫军，杀死卫懿公，攻破都城朝歌。

detail.en: The Zuo Tradition says 730 men and women of the capital survived to cross the Yellow River. It blames Duke Yi, who gave his cranes carriages and ranks, so that soldiers told him to send the cranes to fight. The Di left no account of their own.
detail.zh: 据《左传》，朝歌城里只有730名男女活着渡过黄河。《左传》把失败归咎于卫懿公：他让鹤乘坐大夫的车子，结果士兵们说“让鹤去打仗吧”。狄人自己的说法没有留下来。

summary.en: Qi and its allies build a new walled capital for Wey at Chuqiu.
summary.zh: 齐与盟国为卫国在楚丘筑起新都。

detail.en: For two years the survivors of Chaoge had lived in temporary shelters at Cao. Qi also rebuilt Xing, another state attacked by the Di, at Yiyi in 659 BCE.
detail.zh: 朝歌的幸存者在曹邑的临时住处住了两年。前659年，齐国还在夷仪为同样遭狄人进攻的邢国筑了新城。

summary.en: Qi's coalition of eight states and Chu swear a covenant at Shaoling instead of fighting.
summary.zh: 齐率领的八国联军与楚国在召陵订盟，没有交战。

detail.en: In the Zuo Tradition, Guan Zhong accuses Chu of failing to send the bundles of reeds used to strain the king's sacrificial wine. Chu's envoy replies that if Qi used force, Chu would make its walls a rampart and the Han River a moat.
detail.zh: 据《左传》，管仲责问楚国不向周王进贡用来滤酒的“包茅”。楚国使者回答，如果齐国动武，楚国“方城以为城，汉水以为池”。

summary.en: At Kuiqiu, the Zhou king's envoy honours Duke Huan of Qi with sacrificial meat, and the lords swear a covenant.
summary.zh: 在葵丘，周王的使者把祭肉赐给齐桓公，诸侯订立盟约。

detail.en: Kuiqiu is traditionally placed near present-day Minquan, Henan; some put it in Lankao. The Mencius lists the covenant's oaths, among them not to dam rivers against neighbours and not to stop grain sales in a famine.
detail.zh: 葵丘传统上认为在今河南民权一带，也有人认为在兰考。《孟子》记载的盟誓中，有“无曲防”（不得筑堤坝损害邻国）和“无遏籴”（不得在饥荒时阻止粮食买卖）。

summary.en: Chu defeats Song at the Hong River; Duke Xiang of Song is wounded.
summary.zh: 楚军在泓水击败宋军，宋襄公受伤。

detail.en: The duke would not attack the Chu army while it was crossing the river or before it had formed its ranks. He died of his wound the next year. Some later writers praised his conduct; others mocked it.
detail.zh: 宋襄公不肯在楚军渡河时、列阵前出击，第二年因伤去世。后人对他的做法，有人赞赏，也有人讥笑。

summary.en: Jin, with Qi, Qin and Song, defeats Chu at Chengpu.
summary.zh: 晋联合齐、秦、宋，在城濮击败楚军。

detail.en: Chengpu is traditionally placed south-west of present-day Juancheng, Shandong. According to the Zuo Tradition, Duke Wen first pulled his army back three days' march, keeping a promise made to the King of Chu during his exile. The Chu commander, Ziyu, killed himself after the defeat.
detail.zh: 城濮传统上认为在今山东鄄城西南。据《左传》，晋文公先率军后退三舍，兑现流亡时对楚王许下的诺言。楚军主帅子玉战败后自杀。

summary.en: At Jiantu, Duke Wen of Jin presents his Chu prisoners to the Zhou king and is named leader of the lords.
summary.zh: 在践土，晋文公向周王献上楚国俘虏，被册命为诸侯之长。

detail.en: The Zuo Tradition lists 100 four-horse chariots and 1,000 foot soldiers among the captives presented.
detail.zh: 《左传》记载，献给周王的俘获有披甲的四马战车100乘、步兵1000人。

summary.en: Jin and its Jiang Rong allies ambush a Qin army in the Xiao mountains and capture its three commanders.
summary.zh: 晋军和姜戎在崤山伏击秦军，俘虏三名主将。

detail.en: The Qin force had marched past the Zhou capital to raid Zheng, found Zheng warned, and destroyed the small state of Hua instead. The three commanders were later released at the request of Duke Wen's widow, a Qin princess.
detail.zh: 这支秦军经过周都去偷袭郑国，发现郑国已有防备，便顺手灭了小国滑。被俘的三名秦将，后来因晋文公的遗孀、秦国公主文嬴求情而获释。

summary.en: Duke Mu of Qin turns west against the Rong communities.
summary.zh: 秦穆公转而向西攻打戎人。

detail.en: The Shiji says he 'added twelve states, opened a thousand li of land and became hegemon of the Western Rong', a phrase written from the conqueror's side. The Rong communities' own names and fates are mostly unrecorded.
detail.zh: 《史记》说秦穆公“益国十二，开地千里，遂霸西戎”，这是从征服者一方写的。那些戎人群体自己的名称和遭遇，大多没有记载。

title.en: Deaths at the burial of Duke Mu of Qin

summary.en: 177 people are put to death to accompany Duke Mu of Qin in his tomb at Yong.
summary.zh: 秦穆公葬于雍，从死者177人。

detail.en: Among them were three brothers of the Ziju family, Yanxi, Zhonghang and Zhenhu, mourned in the poem 'Yellow Bird'. Qin had first recorded such deaths for Duke Wu in 678 BCE, with 66 people. The excavated tomb of a later Qin ruler, Duke Jing, at Fengxiang held 186 human victims. Qin abolished the practice in 384 BCE.
detail.zh: 其中有子舆氏的三兄弟奄息、仲行、鍼虎，《诗经·黄鸟》就是哀悼他们的。秦国最早的从死记载是前678年秦武公下葬，从死66人。凤翔发掘的秦景公大墓中，有殉人186具。秦国到前384年才废止从死。

summary.en: King Zhuang of Chu, camped on the Zhou border, asks the royal envoy how heavy the king's bronze cauldrons are.
summary.zh: 楚庄王陈兵周境，向周王的使者打听九鼎的大小轻重。

detail.en: The nine cauldrons stood for the right to rule. The envoy, Wangsun Man, answered that it depended on virtue, not on the cauldrons.
detail.zh: 九鼎象征天下的统治权。周王使者王孙满回答：“在德不在鼎。”

summary.en: Chu defeats Jin beside the Yellow River after besieging Zheng.
summary.zh: 楚军围郑之后，在黄河边的邲击败晋军。

detail.en: The Zuo Tradition says Jin's commanders could not agree whether to fight. In the rush for the boats, men already aboard cut off the fingers of those clinging to the sides, so many that 'they could be scooped up in handfuls'.
detail.zh: 据《左传》，晋军将领对是否出战意见不一。溃退时争抢渡船，船上的人砍断攀住船舷的手指，“舟中之指可掬也”。

summary.en: Jin defeats Chu and Zheng at Yanling; King Gong of Chu is shot in the eye.
summary.zh: 晋军在鄢陵击败楚、郑联军，楚共王被射中眼睛。

detail.en: The Jin archer Lü Qi hit the Chu king in the eye. The Chu commander, Zifan, killed himself after the defeat.
detail.zh: 晋将吕锜射中楚共王的眼睛。楚军主帅子反战败后自杀。

summary.en: At the Song capital, envoys of Jin, Chu and more than ten other states agree to stop fighting.
summary.zh: 在宋都，晋、楚和十几个国家的使臣约定停战。

detail.en: The truce was proposed by Xiang Xu, a minister of Song. Under it, the states allied to Jin also paid court to Chu, and those allied to Chu paid court to Jin.
detail.zh: 停战是宋国大夫向戌倡议的。按照约定，晋的盟国也要朝见楚，楚的盟国也要朝见晋。

summary.en: Wu, with Cai and Tang, defeats Chu at Boju and advances on Ying.
summary.zh: 吴联合蔡、唐，在柏举击败楚军，进逼郢都。

detail.en: Boju is traditionally placed near present-day Macheng, Hubei; another view puts it near Hanchuan. The Zuo Tradition says Wu fought five battles before reaching Ying.
detail.zh: 柏举传统上认为在今湖北麻城一带，另一说在汉川附近。据《左传》，吴军“五战及郢”。

summary.en: Wu troops occupy the Chu capital for months; Wu's commanders move into the royal palaces.
summary.zh: 吴军占领楚都数月，吴国将领住进楚王的宫室。

detail.en: The Guliang Tradition says they also took the wives of the Chu king and his ministers. The Shiji says Wu Zixu dug up King Ping's body and whipped it 300 times; the Zuo Tradition does not. No source counts the people of Ying killed or driven out. Wu withdrew in 505 BCE after Qin sent 500 chariots to help Chu.
detail.zh: 《穀梁传》说，吴人还占有了楚王和大臣的妻妾。《史记》说伍子胥掘出楚平王的尸体，鞭打300下，《左传》没有这样的记载。郢都有多少百姓被杀、逃散，没有任何史料记载。前505年，秦国派战车500乘救楚，吴军撤回。

summary.en: Yue defeats Wu at Zuili; King Helü is wounded and dies.
summary.zh: 越军在檇李击败吴军，吴王阖闾受伤而死。

detail.en: According to the Zuo Tradition, Yue sent three rows of condemned criminals to the front of the Wu lines, where they cut their own throats; while Wu's soldiers stared, Yue attacked. A Yue officer wounded Helü's foot with a dagger-axe.
detail.zh: 据《左传》，越国让三排死刑犯走到吴军阵前当众自刎，趁吴军看呆之际发起进攻。越国大夫灵姑浮用戈击伤了阖闾的脚。

summary.en: Wu defeats Yue; Goujian retreats to Mount Kuaiji with 5,000 armoured men and sues for peace.
summary.zh: 吴军击败越军，勾践带着5000甲兵退守会稽山，向吴求和。

detail.en: Fujiao is traditionally placed on Xishan island in Lake Tai. Wu Zixu urged Fuchai to destroy Yue; the king accepted its submission instead.
detail.zh: 夫椒传统上认为是太湖中的西山岛。伍子胥劝夫差灭掉越国，夫差却接受了越国的求和。

summary.en: Wu digs the Han canal, linking the Yangtze and the Huai.
summary.zh: 吴国开凿邗沟，沟通长江与淮河。

detail.en: The Zuo Tradition says Wu walled the town of Han, near present-day Yangzhou, and cut a channel between the two rivers, the first dated canal in Chinese records. It carried Wu's armies north.
detail.zh: 《左传》说吴国在邗（今扬州附近）筑城，开渠连通江淮，这是中国史书中第一条有确切年份的运河。吴军就沿着它北上。

summary.en: Wu and Lu defeat Qi at Ailing.
summary.zh: 吴、鲁联军在艾陵击败齐军。

detail.en: The Zuo Tradition says the victors captured the Qi commander Guo Shu and 800 chariots, and took the heads of 3,000 armoured soldiers.
detail.zh: 据《左传》，吴、鲁俘获齐军主将国书，缴获战车800乘，斩获甲士首级3000。

summary.en: Fuchai of Wu and the Duke of Jin meet at Huangchi and argue over who should lead the covenant.
summary.zh: 吴王夫差与晋君在黄池会盟，争当盟主。

detail.en: While Fuchai was away, Yue attacked his capital and captured his heir. The Zuo Tradition says Fuchai killed seven men in his own tent to stop the news spreading.
detail.zh: 夫差北上期间，越军攻入吴都，俘虏了吴国太子。据《左传》，夫差为了封锁消息，在帐中亲手杀了七个人。

summary.en: Yue takes the Wu capital, Gusu; Fuchai kills himself.
summary.zh: 越军攻破吴都姑苏，夫差自杀。

detail.en: The Shiji says Goujian offered to settle Fuchai with a hundred households in the east; Fuchai refused, and covered his face before he died so that he would not have to face Wu Zixu among the dead.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，勾践提出把夫差安置到东方，给他一百户人家；夫差拒绝了，临死前蒙住自己的脸，说没脸去见死去的伍子胥。

title.en: Tian Chang kills the Qi ruler

summary.en: Tian Chang kills Duke Jian of Qi; from now on the Tian family controls the state.
summary.zh: 田常杀死齐简公，从此田氏掌握齐国。

detail.en: In 386 BCE the Zhou king recognised Tian He as ruler of Qi; the last ruler of the old Jiang house died in 379 BCE. The map keeps one colour for Qi throughout.
detail.zh: 前386年，周王承认田和为齐国国君；姜姓齐国的最后一位国君死于前379年。地图上齐国始终用同一种颜色。

summary.en: The Zhi, Han and Wei families besiege the Zhao family in their stronghold at Jinyang.
summary.zh: 智、韩、魏三家把赵氏围困在晋阳。

detail.en: The siege went into its third year. In 453 BCE Zhi Bo flooded the city; then Han and Wei changed sides.
detail.zh: 围城进入第三年。前453年智伯引水灌城，随后韩、魏倒戈。

summary.en: Zhi Bo dams the Fen River and floods Jinyang.
summary.zh: 智伯截断汾水，引水灌晋阳城。

detail.en: According to the Shiji, the water rose to within three planks of the top of the walls; people cooked in pots hung up above the water, and families exchanged children to eat. No source says how many people died.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，城墙只剩三版没有被淹，城里“悬釜而炊，易子而食”。死了多少人，没有史料记载。

summary.en: Han, Zhao and Wei turn on the Zhi, kill Zhi Bo and divide his lands.
summary.zh: 韩、赵、魏反攻智氏，杀死智伯，瓜分其领地。

detail.en: They broke the dykes onto the Zhi camp, and the Zhi family was wiped out. The Shiji says Zhao Xiangzi had Zhi Bo's skull lacquered and used it as a drinking cup.
detail.zh: 三家掘开堤防反灌智伯军营，智氏一族被灭。据《史记》，赵襄子把智伯的头骨涂漆，做成饮酒的器具。

title.en: Tomb of Marquis Yi of Zeng

summary.en: Tomb of Marquis Yi of Zeng near Suizhou, buried about 433 BCE and excavated in 1978.
summary.zh: 随州附近的曾侯乙墓，约前433年下葬，1978年发掘。

detail.en: It held a set of 65 bronze bells, one of them a gift from the King of Chu dated to about 433 BCE, and the coffins of 21 young women killed to accompany the marquis. Inscriptions found since show that Zeng was the state the texts call Sui.
detail.zh: 墓中出土青铜编钟65件，其中一件是楚王所赠，铭文年代约为前433年；还有21具殉葬年轻女子的棺木。后来出土的铭文表明，曾国就是史书中的随国。

summary.en: King Weilie of Zhou recognises Han, Zhao and Wei as regional states.
summary.zh: 周威烈王承认韩、赵、魏为诸侯。

detail.en: Sima Guang began his Zizhi tongjian with this year, as the moment the Zhou order broke. The borders between Han, Zhao and Wei on this frame are borrowed from a map of 350 BCE.
detail.zh: 司马光的《资治通鉴》从这一年写起，把它看作周代秩序崩坏的开端。这一帧中韩、赵、魏之间的分界，借用的是前350年地图的画法。

summary.en: Han, Zhao and Wei depose the last Duke of Jin and divide his remaining lands.
summary.zh: 韩、赵、魏废黜晋国最后一位国君，瓜分晋君剩下的土地。

detail.en: The Shiji says Duke Jing of Jin was made a commoner and the sacrifices of Jin's ruling house came to an end.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，晋静公被废为平民，晋国公室的祭祀从此断绝。

summary.en: Marquis Wen of Wei comes to power and employs reformers such as Li Kui and Wu Qi.
summary.zh: 魏文侯即位，任用李悝、吴起等人推行改革。

detail.en: The year 445 BCE follows the corrected chronology of Yang Kuan; the Shiji's dates for Marquis Wen are about twenty years later. Anyi, the early Wei capital, is in the south of present-day Shanxi.
detail.zh: 前445年是采用杨宽校订的年代；《史记》所记魏文侯的年代晚了约二十年。魏国早期都城安邑，在今山西南部。

summary.en: Duke Xian of Qin abolishes the practice of killing people to accompany a ruler in death.
summary.zh: 秦献公下令废止为君主殉葬的从死制度。

detail.en: The Qin annals record it in his first year in three words: 'stopped following in death'.
detail.zh: 《秦本纪》只用了三个字记载这件事：“止从死”。

summary.en: Nobles shoot Wu Qi at the funeral of King Dao of Chu; the new king executes more than seventy noble families in return.
summary.zh: 贵族们在楚悼王的葬礼上射杀吴起；新即位的楚王诛灭了七十多家贵族。

detail.en: According to the Shiji, Wu Qi threw himself on the king's body, so the arrows also struck the corpse; that was the crime for which the families were killed.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，吴起扑到楚悼王的遗体上，乱箭也射中了王尸；这些贵族家族就是因此获罪被灭的。

summary.en: Qin defeats Wei at Shimen; the Qin annals record 60,000 heads taken.
summary.zh: 秦在石门击败魏军，《秦本纪》记斩首六万。

detail.en: The Qin annals name Qin's opponent as Jin, meaning Wei, and say the Zhou king sent Qin embroidered robes in congratulation. Shimen is traditionally placed in the south of present-day Shanxi. The number is Qin's own count.
detail.zh: 《秦本纪》称对手为“晋”，实指魏国，并说周王赐给秦君礼服以示祝贺。石门传统上认为在今山西南部。这个数字是秦国自己的记录。

summary.en: Shang Yang's first laws in Qin: households grouped and made answerable for each other, rewards for farming and for heads taken in battle.
summary.zh: 商鞅在秦国颁布第一批新法：编组户籍、相互连坐，奖励耕作和斩获敌首。

detail.en: The Shiji says anyone who failed to denounce a crime was to be cut in two at the waist, and anyone who denounced one was rewarded like a soldier who had taken a head in battle. A household with two adult sons who did not set up separate homes paid double tax.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，知情不告发的人处以腰斩，告发的人与斩获敌首同赏；家中有两个以上成年男子而不分家的，赋税加倍。

summary.en: Shen Buhai serves as chief minister of Han.
summary.zh: 申不害任韩国国相。

detail.en: He taught that a ruler should control officials by comparing their words with their results. The Shiji says that while he lived, Han was well governed and no state attacked it.
detail.zh: 他主张君主要通过核对官吏的言论与实绩来驾驭他们。据《史记》，申不害在世时，韩国政治安定，没有国家来侵犯。

summary.en: Qin moves its capital to Xianyang, groups its villages into counties under appointed magistrates and redraws field boundaries.
summary.zh: 秦迁都咸阳，把乡邑合并为县，由国君委派县令治理，并重新划定田界。

detail.en: The Shang Yang biography counts 31 counties, the Qin annals 41. In 344 BCE Shang Yang issued standard measures; one survives in the Shanghai Museum.
detail.zh: 《商君列传》说共31县，《秦本纪》说41县。前344年商鞅颁行标准量器，其中一件今藏上海博物馆。

title.en: Shang Yang and his family killed

summary.en: After Duke Xiao's death, Shang Yang is accused of rebellion, killed and torn apart by chariots; his family is put to death.
summary.zh: 秦孝公死后，商鞅被控谋反，被杀后车裂示众，全家被处死。

detail.en: The Shiji says that when he fled, an innkeeper turned him away because Shang Yang's own law punished anyone who lodged a guest without papers. His laws stayed in force.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，商鞅逃亡时，客店不敢收留他，因为按照商鞅自己定的法令，留宿没有凭证的客人要受罚。他的新法仍然施行。

summary.en: Qi defeats Wei at Guiling while Wei is besieging the Zhao capital.
summary.zh: 魏军围攻赵都时，齐军在桂陵击败魏军。

detail.en: Guiling is traditionally placed near present-day Changyuan, Henan; another view puts it near Heze, Shandong. Qi marched on the Wei capital rather than on Handan, the origin of the saying 'besiege Wei to save Zhao'.
detail.zh: 桂陵传统上认为在今河南长垣一带，另一说在山东菏泽附近。齐军不去邯郸而直扑魏都，这就是“围魏救赵”的由来。

summary.en: Qi ambushes Wei at Maling; Wei's crown prince is captured and its general Pang Juan dies.
summary.zh: 齐军在马陵伏击魏军，魏太子申被俘，魏将庞涓身死。

detail.en: Maling is traditionally placed on the border of present-day Shen county, Shandong, and Fan county, Henan; another view puts it at Tancheng. Some chronologies date the battle to 341 BCE. The Yinqueshan slips say Pang Juan was captured at Guiling, not killed at Maling.
detail.zh: 马陵传统上认为在今山东莘县、河南范县交界一带，另一说在郯城。也有年表把这次战役定在前341年。银雀山竹简则说，庞涓是在桂陵被擒的，并非死于马陵。

summary.en: A coalition of Chu, Wei, Zhao, Han and Yan attacks Qin and turns back.
summary.zh: 楚、魏、赵、韩、燕五国联军攻秦，无功而返。

detail.en: The Shiji names King Huai of Chu as leader of the alliance. Han and Zhao did most of the fighting, and lost at Xiuyu the next year.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，楚怀王是这次合纵的“纵长”。实际作战的主要是韩、赵两国，第二年它们在修鱼战败。

summary.en: Qin defeats the armies of Han and Zhao at Xiuyu; the Qin annals record 82,000 heads.
summary.zh: 秦军在修鱼击败韩、赵联军，《秦本纪》记斩首八万二千。

detail.en: The Qin annals put the battle in 318 BCE, the year of the coalition; many modern chronologies date it 317 BCE. Xiuyu is traditionally placed south-west of present-day Yuanyang, Henan. The number is Qin's own count.
detail.zh: 《秦本纪》把这次战役记在合纵攻秦的前318年，现代许多年表定为前317年。修鱼传统上认为在今河南原阳西南。这个数字是秦国自己的记录。

summary.en: A Qin army under Sima Cuo crosses the Qinling mountains and conquers Shu, then Ba.
summary.zh: 司马错率秦军翻越秦岭，灭蜀，接着灭巴。

detail.en: Shu, centred on the Chengdu plain, had a bronze culture of its own, known from sites such as Sanxingdui and Jinsha. The Huayang guozhi says the Shu king was defeated at Jiameng and killed at Wuyang.
detail.zh: 以成都平原为中心的蜀国，有自己独特的青铜文化，三星堆、金沙等遗址就是证明。据《华阳国志》，蜀王在葭萌战败，逃到武阳被秦军杀死。

summary.en: Qin defeats Chu at Danyang and captures its commander Qu Gai; the Qin annals record 80,000 heads.
summary.zh: 秦军在丹阳击败楚军，俘虏楚将屈丐，《秦本纪》记斩首八万。

detail.en: Danyang is traditionally placed north of the Dan River near present-day Xichuan, Henan. Qin then took Chu's Hanzhong. The war followed Zhang Yi's broken promise of 600 li of land.
detail.zh: 丹阳传统上认为在今河南淅川一带的丹水以北。秦随后夺取了楚国的汉中。这场战争起因于张仪许诺割地六百里而又食言。

summary.en: Chu's counter-attack reaches Lantian, close to the Qin capital, and is defeated.
summary.zh: 楚军反攻，打到离秦都不远的蓝田，又被击败。

detail.en: Han and Wei then attacked Chu from behind, reaching Deng, and Chu withdrew.
detail.zh: 这时韩、魏从背后袭击楚国，一直打到邓，楚军只得撤回。

summary.en: Qin takes Han's walled city of Yiyang; the Qin annals record 60,000 heads.
summary.zh: 秦攻下韩国的宜阳城，《秦本纪》记斩首六万。

detail.en: Yiyang opened Qin's road east to the Zhou capital. The same year King Wu of Qin, visiting Zhou, broke his leg lifting a bronze cauldron and died.
detail.zh: 攻下宜阳，秦国东通周都的道路就打开了。同一年，秦武王在周都举鼎，压断了腿骨而死。

summary.en: Zhao conquers Zhongshan and moves its king to Fushi in the far north.
summary.zh: 赵灭中山，把中山王迁到北方的肤施。

detail.en: Zhongshan was founded by people Zhou texts called the White Di. Its royal tombs at Pingshan, Hebei, excavated in the 1970s, held long bronze inscriptions and a bronze plan of the king's burial ground.
detail.zh: 中山国由周人文献所称的白狄人建立。1970年代在河北平山发掘的中山王墓，出土了铭文很长的青铜器和一块铜制的陵园平面图。

summary.en: Bai Qi defeats Han and Wei at Yique, south of Luoyang; Qin records 240,000 heads.
summary.zh: 白起在洛阳以南的伊阙击败韩、魏联军，秦方记录斩首二十四万。

detail.en: Both the Qin annals and Bai Qi's biography give 240,000 heads and the capture of the Wei commander Gongsun Xi. This is Qin's own count; no Han or Wei record survives.
detail.zh: 《秦本纪》和《白起列传》都记斩首二十四万，俘虏魏将公孙喜。这是秦国自己的记录，韩、魏方面的记录没有留下来。

summary.en: Yan, Qin, Han, Zhao and Wei defeat Qi west of the Ji River; Yue Yi takes Linzi.
summary.zh: 燕、秦、韩、赵、魏五国在济水以西大败齐军，乐毅攻入临淄。

detail.en: Only Ju and Jimo held out. King Min of Qi fled to Ju, where the Chu general Nao Chi, sent to help him, killed him. Yue Yi is credited with taking more than 70 cities.
detail.zh: 齐国只剩下莒和即墨两城。齐湣王逃到莒，被前来“救援”的楚将淖齿杀死。乐毅前后攻下齐国七十多城。

summary.en: Wei besieges and takes Handan, the Zhao capital.
summary.zh: 魏军围攻并占领赵都邯郸。

detail.en: Wei held the city until 351 BCE, when it handed it back to Zhao under a peace agreement.
detail.zh: 魏国占据邯郸到前351年，双方议和后才把城还给赵国。

summary.en: Qi invades Yan during its civil war and occupies the country.
summary.zh: 齐国趁燕国内乱出兵，占领燕国。

detail.en: The civil war over King Kuai's abdication had already killed tens of thousands, the Shiji says. Mencius told the King of Qi that his troops were killing fathers and elder brothers, binding sons and younger brothers, destroying ancestral temples and carrying off sacred vessels. Yan's people rose and Qi withdrew.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，燕王哙让位引起的内乱已经“死者数万”。孟子对齐王说，齐军在燕国“杀其父兄，系累其子弟，毁其宗庙，迁其重器”。燕人起来反抗，齐军撤走。

title.en: Zhao adopts northern dress and mounted archery

summary.en: King Wuling of Zhao orders his soldiers to wear northern dress and fight as mounted archers.
summary.zh: 赵武灵王下令士兵改穿胡服，练习骑射。

detail.en: The Shiji records long arguments at court about giving up Huaxia dress. Zhao then expanded into the lands of the Linhu and Loufan, whose own accounts do not survive.
detail.zh: 《史记》记载了赵国朝廷围绕放弃华夏服饰的长篇争论。此后赵国向林胡、楼烦的地方扩张，这些人群自己的记载没有留下来。

summary.en: The Jixia gate of Linzi, where the kings of Qi paid scholars of many schools to live and debate.
summary.zh: 临淄的稷门一带，齐王供养各派学者在这里居住、辩论。

detail.en: The Shiji says King Xuan of Qi gave 76 scholars houses and the rank of senior official, 'not to govern but to debate'. Mencius and Xunzi both spent time in Qi.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，齐宣王给76位学者赐宅第、封上大夫，让他们“不治而议论”。孟子、荀子都曾在齐国停留。

summary.en: Bai Qi floods the Chu city of Yan; a much later source says hundreds of thousands drowned.
summary.zh: 白起水灌楚国鄢城；一部晚出的文献说淹死者达数十万。

detail.en: The Shiji records only that Qin took Yan. The Shuijing zhu, written about 800 years later, says the water broke into the north-east of the city and that 'several hundred thousand' people died east of it, so that the pond there was called the Stinking Pool. Its figure cannot be checked.
detail.zh: 《史记》只记秦攻取鄢城。约800年后成书的《水经注》说，大水从城东北角冲入，百姓随水漂流，死在城东的有“数十万”，那里的水塘因此叫“臭池”。这个数字无从核实。

summary.en: Bai Qi takes Ying, the Chu capital, and burns the royal tombs at Yiling.
summary.zh: 白起攻占楚都郢，焚烧夷陵的楚王陵墓。

detail.en: Qin made the area its Nan commandery, and the Chu court moved north-east to Chen. The 260 and 230 BCE frames of this map still show the area as Chu, because they keep the outlines of a 280 BCE source map.
detail.zh: 秦在这里设立南郡，楚国朝廷东迁到陈。这张地图前260年和前230年两帧仍把这一带画作楚国，因为它们沿用的是前280年来源地图的轮廓。

summary.en: Tian Dan breaks out of Jimo and drives the Yan army out of Qi.
summary.zh: 田单从即墨出击，把燕军赶出齐国。

detail.en: The Shiji says he tied blades to the horns of more than a thousand oxen and set fire to reeds tied to their tails, then attacked at night. Qi recovered more than 70 cities.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，田单在一千多头牛的角上绑上刀，尾巴上绑上浸油的芦苇点火，趁夜冲向燕军。齐国收复了七十多城。

summary.en: During the siege of Jimo, Yan troops cut off the noses of Qi prisoners and dig up and burn the dead in the town's graves.
summary.zh: 围攻即墨期间，燕军割掉被俘齐兵的鼻子，又挖开城外坟墓、焚烧尸体。

detail.en: The Shiji tells this as the result of rumours spread by Tian Dan to enrage the defenders, so the episode may be shaped by the storyteller. It is recorded in the same plain terms as Qi's conduct in Yan in 314 BCE.
detail.zh: 《史记》把这些事写成田单故意散布谣言、激燕军所为，可能经过讲述者的加工。它的写法，与前314年齐军在燕国的行为一样平实。

summary.en: Bai Qi defeats Wei and Zhao at Huayang.
summary.zh: 白起在华阳击败魏、赵联军。

detail.en: Bai Qi's biography gives 130,000 heads; the Qin annals give 150,000 and date the battle a year earlier. These are Qin's own counts.
detail.zh: 《白起列传》记斩首十三万；《秦本纪》记斩首十五万，并把这一战记早一年。这些都是秦国自己的记录。

summary.en: After Huayang, Qin's army drowns 20,000 Zhao soldiers in the Yellow River.
summary.zh: 华阳之战后，秦军把两万名赵国士兵沉入黄河。

detail.en: Bai Qi's biography says that after fighting the Zhao commander Jia Yan, Qin 'sank 20,000 of his men in the river'. The figure comes from the Qin side, and the exact place is not recorded.
detail.zh: 《白起列传》说，与赵将贾偃交战后，秦军“沈其卒二万人于河中”。这个数字来自秦方，具体地点没有记载。

summary.en: Zhao She defeats a Qin army besieging Yuyu.
summary.zh: 赵奢击败围攻阏与的秦军。

detail.en: Yuyu is traditionally placed near present-day Heshun, Shanxi; another view puts it near Wu'an, Hebei. The Zhao annals date the battle to 270 BCE. The Shiji says Zhao She fortified his camp and waited 28 days before striking.
detail.zh: 阏与传统上认为在今山西和顺一带，另一说在河北武安附近。《赵世家》把这一战记在前270年。据《史记》，赵奢先筑营坚守二十八天，然后突然出击。

summary.en: Cut off from Han, the governor of Shangdang, Feng Ting, offers its seventeen walled towns to Zhao, which accepts.
summary.zh: 上党与韩国本土的联系被切断，郡守冯亭把十七座城邑献给赵国，赵国接受了。

detail.en: Some Zhao advisers warned that accepting the gift would bring war with Qin. Two years later the armies met at Changping.
detail.zh: 赵国有大臣警告，接受上党会招来秦国的进攻。两年后，秦赵两军在长平决战。

summary.en: Qin defeats Zhao after a three-year campaign around Changping; the surrounded Zhao army surrenders.
summary.zh: 秦赵在长平一带相持三年，秦军最终获胜，被围的赵军投降。

detail.en: Zhao's general Lian Po held fortified lines. In 260 BCE Zhao replaced him with Zhao Kuo, and Qin secretly sent Bai Qi, who cut the Zhao army off. After 46 days without food, the Shiji says, the soldiers were killing and eating one another. Zhao Kuo died trying to break out. Bai Qi later said that more than half of Qin's own soldiers had died.
detail.zh: 赵将廉颇筑垒坚守。前260年，赵国改派赵括为将，秦国则秘密起用白起，切断了赵军的退路和粮道。据《史记》，赵军断粮46天，士兵“内阴相杀食”。赵括率军突围时战死。白起后来说，秦军自己也“死者过半”。

title.en: Killing of the Zhao prisoners at Changping

summary.en: After the surrender at Changping, Bai Qi has the Zhao prisoners killed and buried, sending 240 of the youngest home. The Shiji gives about 400,000 dead.
summary.zh: 长平投降后，白起下令坑杀赵军降卒，只放回240名年少者。《史记》记死者约40万。

detail.en: Bai Qi's biography says 400,000 surrendered and gives 450,000 'beheaded or captured' in the whole campaign; the Qin annals say 'more than 400,000, all killed'. These are Qin's own counts and are disputed. A pit excavated at Yonglu in 1995 held the jumbled remains of about 130 men, many with cut wounds or arrowheads; the excavators concluded most were killed and then thrown in, not buried alive. Most of the dead have no names.
detail.zh: 《白起列传》说降卒40万人，全役“前后斩首虏四十五万人”；《秦本纪》说“四十余万尽杀之”。这些都是秦方的记录，学界有争议。1995年在永录村发掘的一个尸骨坑里，杂乱地埋着约130名男子的遗骸，许多带有砍伤或箭伤；发掘者认为，他们大多是被杀后扔进坑里的，并非活埋。死者大多没有留下姓名。

summary.en: Qin besieges Handan; with relief armies from Wei and Chu, Zhao holds out.
summary.zh: 秦军围攻邯郸；在魏、楚援军帮助下，赵国守住了都城。

detail.en: Inside the city, a Zhao official told Lord Pingyuan, people were 'burning bones for fuel and exchanging children to eat'. Lord Xinling of Wei had his king's tiger tally stolen and the Wei commander Jin Bi killed with an iron mallet, so that he could lead Jin Bi's army to Handan.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，城中有人对平原君说，邯郸百姓已经“炊骨易子而食”。魏国的信陵君让人盗出魏王的虎符，又让朱亥用铁锤打死魏将晋鄙，夺了他的军队来救邯郸。

summary.en: Bai Qi, who had refused to lead the attack on Handan, is stripped of rank and ordered to kill himself.
summary.zh: 白起因拒绝率军攻打邯郸，被削去爵位，赐死。

detail.en: The Shiji has him say before he died: 'At Changping several hundred thousand Zhao soldiers surrendered, and I deceived them and buried them all. That alone is enough for me to deserve death.'
detail.zh: 据《史记》，白起临死前说：“长平之战，赵卒降者数十万人，我诈而尽阬之，是足以死。”

summary.en: Qin takes the Western Zhou domain; King Nan, the last Zhou king, dies.
summary.zh: 秦攻取西周，最后一位周王周赧王去世。

detail.en: The neighbouring Eastern Zhou domain held out until 249 BCE. The Qin annals say the people of Zhou fled east and the nine cauldrons were taken to Qin.
detail.zh: 相邻的东周一直存在到前249年。据《秦本纪》，周的百姓向东逃散，九鼎被运到秦国。

summary.en: Zhao, Chu, Wei, Han and Yan attack Qin for the last time and are driven back.
summary.zh: 赵、楚、魏、韩、燕最后一次合纵攻秦，被秦军击退。

detail.en: The Zhao annals say the allied armies reached Zui, close to the Qin capital; the biography of Lord Chunshen says they turned back at the Hangu pass. The point marks Zui, near present-day Lintong.
detail.zh: 《赵世家》说联军打到了离秦都不远的蕞，《春申君列传》却说联军到函谷关就退回了。图上的点标在蕞，即今临潼一带。

summary.en: Qin's general Huan Yi defeats Zhao at Pingyang and kills its commander Hu Zhe; Qin's annals record 100,000 heads.
summary.zh: 秦将桓齮在平阳击败赵军，杀死赵将扈辄，秦方记录斩首十万。

detail.en: Pingyang is traditionally placed west of present-day Linzhang, Hebei. The figure is Qin's own count.
detail.zh: 平阳传统上认为在今河北临漳以西。这个数字是秦国自己的记录。

summary.en: The Zhao general Li Mu routs a Qin army at Fei.
summary.zh: 赵将李牧在肥大败秦军。

detail.en: Fei is traditionally placed near present-day Jinzhou, Hebei. Zhao made Li Mu Lord Wu'an for the victory; four years later it executed him.
detail.zh: 肥传统上认为在今河北晋州一带。赵国因此战封李牧为武安君；四年后，赵国却杀了他。

summary.en: Qin's Neishi Teng captures King An of Han; Han becomes Qin's Yingchuan commandery.
summary.zh: 秦内史腾俘虏韩王安，韩国成为秦的颍川郡。

detail.en: Han was the first of the six to fall. In 226 BCE people at the old Han capital, Xinzheng, rose against Qin.
detail.zh: 韩是六国中第一个灭亡的。前226年，韩国旧都新郑的人起来反抗秦国。

summary.en: Qin takes Handan and captures King Qian of Zhao.
summary.zh: 秦军攻下邯郸，俘虏赵王迁。

detail.en: The Qin king came to Handan and had everyone who had wronged his mother's family killed and buried in pits. Zhao's prince Jia escaped to Dai, in the north, and reigned there until 222 BCE.
detail.zh: 秦王亲自来到邯郸，把与他母家有仇怨的人全部坑杀。赵公子嘉逃到北方的代地称王，一直坚持到前222年。

summary.en: A Qin army of 200,000 under Li Xin and Meng Tian is routed by the Chu general Xiang Yan.
summary.zh: 李信、蒙恬率领的二十万秦军，被楚将项燕击溃。

detail.en: The Shiji says the Chu army followed for three days and nights without rest, broke into two Qin camps and killed seven commandants. The text gives no year; 225 BCE is inferred. Chengfu, where the rout began, is traditionally placed near present-day Bozhou, Anhui; some scholars put it at Fucheng in Henan.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，楚军尾随秦军三天三夜不停歇，攻破两座营垒，杀死七名都尉。原文没有年份，前225年是推定的。溃败开始的城父，传统上认为在今安徽亳州附近，也有学者认为是河南的父城。

summary.en: Wang Jian's army of 600,000 conquers Chu; King Fuchu is captured and Xiang Yan dies.
summary.zh: 王翦率六十万大军灭楚，俘虏楚王负刍，项燕身死。

detail.en: The Shiji's chapters disagree on the order. The Chu annals put Xiang Yan's death in 224 BCE and the king's capture in 223 BCE; the First Emperor's annals put the capture first and have Xiang Yan make Lord Changping king before both died in 223 BCE. Wang Jian finished conquering the lands south of the Yangtze in 222 BCE.
detail.zh: 《史记》各篇记载的次序不同。《楚世家》说前224年项燕被杀，前223年楚王被俘；《秦始皇本纪》说秦军先俘虏楚王，项燕又拥立昌平君为王，两人都死于前223年。前222年，王翦攻取了长江以南的楚地。

summary.en: Wang Ben captures King Xi of Yan in Liaodong, then the Zhao prince Jia in Dai.
summary.zh: 王贲在辽东俘虏燕王喜，又在代地俘虏赵公子嘉。

detail.en: Ji, the Yan capital, had fallen in 226 BCE. The king had fled east, after sending Qin the head of his own son, Crown Prince Dan, who had sent Jing Ke.
detail.zh: 燕都蓟在前226年已经陷落。燕王喜逃往辽东，此前还把派荆轲行刺的太子丹斩首，献给了秦国。

summary.en: Work begins on a canal from the Jing River across the plain north of the Wei, designed by the Han engineer Zheng Guo.
summary.zh: 韩国水工郑国主持修建的引泾水渠开工，灌溉渭水以北的平原。

detail.en: The Shiji says Han sent Zheng Guo to wear Qin out with a huge project. When the plot was discovered he argued that the canal would still serve Qin, and it was finished; it watered more than 40,000 qing of salty land.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，韩国派郑国来秦修渠，本想用浩大的工程拖垮秦国。计谋败露后，郑国说这条渠修成了对秦国仍然有利，于是工程得以完成，灌溉了四万多顷盐碱地。

summary.en: Han Fei, the Han prince and writer on government, dies in prison in Qin.
summary.zh: 韩国公子、政论家韩非死在秦国狱中。

detail.en: The Shiji says Li Si, who had studied with him under Xunzi, had him imprisoned and sent him poison; the king's pardon came too late.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，曾与他一同师从荀子的李斯把他下狱，又送去毒药；秦王后悔想赦免他时，韩非已经死了。

title.en: Jing Ke's attempt on the King of Qin

summary.en: Jing Ke, sent by Crown Prince Dan of Yan, tries to stab the King of Qin at court and is killed.
summary.zh: 燕太子丹派荆轲在秦廷行刺秦王，荆轲失败被杀。

detail.en: The Shiji and the Zhanguoce tell the story in literary form, including the farewell song at the Yi River. The attempt led Qin to attack Yan the next year.
detail.zh: 《史记》和《战国策》以文学化的笔法讲述了这个故事，包括易水送别时的歌。行刺失败后，秦第二年就出兵攻燕。

summary.en: Wang Ben diverts canal water into Daliang; the walls fall and King Jia of Wei surrenders.
summary.zh: 王贲引河沟之水灌大梁，城墙被泡塌，魏王假投降。

detail.en: People living at the ruins later told Sima Qian that the siege lasted three months. No source gives the number of townspeople who died.
detail.zh: 后来住在大梁废墟附近的人告诉司马迁，水灌大梁历时三个月。城中死了多少百姓，没有史料记载。

summary.en: The people of Daliang, the Wei capital, are trapped for three months as the floodwater rises against the walls.
summary.zh: 魏都大梁的百姓被困城中三个月，大水一直漫到城墙。

detail.en: Like Jinyang in 453 BCE and Yan in 279 BCE, the flooding struck everyone inside the walls. The Shiji records the king's surrender, not the deaths.
detail.zh: 与前453年的晋阳、前279年的鄢城一样，大水淹到的是城里所有的人。《史记》记下了魏王投降，却没有记下死者。

summary.en: Wang Ben's army marches south from Yan; King Jian of Qi surrenders without fighting.
summary.zh: 王贲从燕地南下，齐王建不战而降。

detail.en: The Shiji says the minister Hou Sheng, paid by Qin agents, had kept Qi out of the alliances for decades. King Jian was moved to Gong, and a Qi song blamed him for the kingdom's fall.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，齐相后胜收受了秦国的贿赂，几十年来一直让齐国置身于合纵之外。齐王建被迁到共，齐人编歌埋怨他亡了国。

summary.en: The King of Qin takes the new title huangdi, 'emperor', and calls himself the First Emperor.
summary.zh: 秦王采用“皇帝”这一新称号，自称始皇帝。

detail.en: The empire was divided into 36 commanderies. Weapons from all the conquered states were melted down into twelve bronze figures, and writing, weights, measures and axle widths were standardised.
detail.zh: 全国分为36郡。收缴各国的兵器，熔铸成十二个铜人；文字、度量衡和车轨宽度都统一了标准。

summary.en: Meng Tian's army drives the Xiongnu out of the Ordos, inside the great bend of the Yellow River, and Qin builds walls along the new frontier.
summary.zh: 蒙恬率军把匈奴逐出黄河河套以南，沿新边界修筑长城。

detail.en: The Shiji says Meng Tian commanded 300,000 men. His wall joined older walls built by Qin, Zhao and Yan. No Xiongnu account of the war survives.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，蒙恬率军三十万。他修的长城，连接了秦、赵、燕三国原有的长城。匈奴一方对这场战争的说法没有留下来。

summary.en: Qin armies conquer Lingnan, in the far south, and set up the commanderies of Nanhai, Guilin and Xiang.
summary.zh: 秦军攻取岭南，设立南海、桂林、象郡三郡。

detail.en: The First Emperor's annals say the troops included men who had fled their debts, men who had married into their wives' families, and merchants, all sent by order. This conquest is not drawn on the map.
detail.zh: 据《秦始皇本纪》，南征的兵员中有曾经逃亡的人、入赘的女婿和商人，都是被强制征发的。这次扩张没有画在地图上。

summary.en: The Lingqu canal links the Xiang River, which flows to the Yangtze, with the Li River, which flows south.
summary.zh: 灵渠沟通北流入长江的湘江和南流的漓江。

detail.en: It was cut to carry supplies to the Qin armies in Lingnan. The canal visible today has been rebuilt many times.
detail.zh: 灵渠是为了给岭南的秦军运送粮草而开凿的。今天看到的灵渠经过历代多次重修。

summary.en: On Li Si's proposal, the emperor orders histories other than Qin's, and private copies of the Odes, the Documents and the writings of the Hundred Schools, to be burned.
summary.zh: 秦始皇采纳李斯的建议，下令焚毁秦国以外的史书，以及民间收藏的《诗》《书》和百家著作。

detail.en: Copies held by court scholars and books on medicine, divination and farming were exempt. Anyone discussing the Odes and Documents was to be executed in public; anyone using the past to criticise the present, killed with his family; anyone who had not burned his books 30 days after the order, tattooed and sent to labour on the walls.
detail.zh: 朝廷博士官所藏的书，以及医药、卜筮、种树之书，不在焚毁之列。敢私下谈论《诗》《书》的，处死示众；以古非今的，灭族；命令下达三十天仍不烧书的，脸上刺字，罚去修城。

title.en: Killing of the scholars at Xianyang

summary.en: After two court magicians criticise him and flee, the First Emperor has more than 460 scholars in Xianyang killed and buried.
summary.zh: 两名方士批评秦始皇后逃走，秦始皇下令坑杀咸阳的460多名“诸生”。

detail.en: The Shiji calls the victims zhusheng, 'the scholars', and elsewhere 'magicians'; the emperor's son Fusu protested that they 'all recite and follow Confucius'. Some historians argue that the later phrase 'burying the Confucians' was shaped by Han writers; others defend the Shiji's account. The number is the Shiji's.
detail.zh: 《秦始皇本纪》称死者为“诸生”，《儒林列传》说是“术士”；始皇长子扶苏劝谏说他们“皆诵法孔子”。有学者认为“坑儒”的说法是汉代人塑造的，也有学者维护《史记》的记载。人数出自《史记》。

title.en: Forced labour on the emperor's tomb

summary.en: More than 700,000 convicts and castrated prisoners are put to work on the Epang palace and the emperor's tomb at Mount Li.
summary.zh: 七十多万受过宫刑和其他刑罚的刑徒，被分派去修建阿房宫和骊山陵墓。

detail.en: At Zhaobeihu, west of the tomb, archaeologists found 114 labourers' graves in 1979–80. Tiles from them carry the names of 19 of the dead, such as Qingji of Dongwu, who held the rank shangzao and was working off a debt. How many died building the tomb is not known.
detail.zh: 1979至1980年，考古人员在陵西的赵背户村探出修陵人墓葬114座。墓中残瓦刻有19名死者的名字，如“东武居赀上造庆忌”：东武人庆忌，爵位上造，以劳役抵债。修陵死了多少人，没有记载。

summary.en: The First Emperor dies at Shaqiu on his last tour; Zhao Gao and Li Si hide his death and forge orders for Fusu and Meng Tian to kill themselves.
summary.zh: 秦始皇在最后一次出巡途中死于沙丘；赵高、李斯秘不发丧，伪造诏书逼扶苏、蒙恬自杀。

detail.en: The Shiji says they carried the body back to Xianyang in a closed carriage, with a cartload of salted fish to hide the smell.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，他们用密闭的车子把遗体运回咸阳，又让车队装上一石鲍鱼，掩盖尸体的气味。

summary.en: Conscripts led by Chen Sheng and Wu Guang, held up by rain on their way to the northern frontier, rise in revolt at Dazexiang.
summary.zh: 陈胜、吴广率领被大雨耽误行程的戍卒，在大泽乡起事。

detail.en: The Shiji says the penalty for arriving late was death. Qin laws found at Shuihudi set fines, not death, for lateness in labour service, so historians debate this detail.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，戍卒误期按律当斩。睡虎地出土的秦律对服徭役误期只规定罚款，因此史家对这一细节有不同看法。

summary.en: Ziying, the last ruler of Qin, surrenders to Liu Bang outside Xianyang.
summary.zh: 秦王子婴在咸阳城外向刘邦投降。

detail.en: Weeks later Xiang Yu entered Xianyang, killed Ziying and burned the palaces. Because the Qin year began in the tenth month, some reckon the surrender as 207 BCE.
detail.zh: 几个星期后，项羽进入咸阳，杀死子婴，焚烧宫室。由于秦历以十月为岁首，也有人把子婴投降算在前207年。

summary.en: The First Emperor's tomb at Mount Li, near present-day Xi'an, with the pits of the terracotta army found in 1974.
summary.zh: 骊山脚下的秦始皇陵，在今西安附近；1974年在这里发现了兵马俑坑。

detail.en: UNESCO listed the mausoleum as World Heritage in 1987. The tomb mound itself has not been excavated.
detail.zh: 1987年秦始皇陵列入联合国教科文组织《世界遗产名录》。陵墓封土本身至今没有发掘。

summary.en: The Dujiangyan irrigation works on the Min River, begun by Li Bing, Qin's governor of Shu, in the third century BCE.
summary.zh: 岷江上的都江堰水利工程，由秦国蜀郡守李冰在前3世纪主持兴建。

detail.en: The Shiji says the governor of Shu cut channels to tame the river and water the Chengdu plain. The works still irrigate the plain; UNESCO listed them in 2000.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，蜀郡守开凿渠道，平息水患，灌溉成都平原。都江堰至今仍在灌溉农田，2000年列入《世界遗产名录》。

summary.en: The Second Emperor of Qin deposes Lord Jiao, the last ruler of Wey, and makes him a commoner.
summary.zh: 秦二世废卫君角为庶人。

detail.en: Wey, by then a small dependency at Yewang, had outlived every other Zhou state; with this its ancestral sacrifices ended.
detail.zh: 这时的卫国只是迁居野王的一个附庸小国，却比其他周代诸侯国存在得都久；到这时，卫国宗庙的祭祀断绝了。

summary.en: Chu defeats Yue and kills its king, Wujiang; Yue's royal family breaks up into small chiefdoms along the coast.
summary.zh: 楚国击败越国，杀死越王无疆；越国王族分散到沿海各地，各自称王称君。

detail.en: The Shiji gives no year. It links the war to King Wei of Chu, which would mean about 333 BCE; Yang Kuan dates it to 306 BCE. In 222 BCE Qin 'brought the Yue lords to submission'.
detail.zh: 《史记》没有记年份。它把这场战争系于楚威王时，约在前333年；杨宽则定在前306年。前222年，秦“降越君”。

title.en: King Ping of Zhou 周平王

summary.en: King of Zhou, r. 770–720 BCE. Son of King You; tradition dates the Zhou court's move east to Chengzhou (Luoyang) to his first year, the start of the Eastern Zhou.
summary.zh: 周王，前770—前720年在位，周幽王之子。传统说法把周室东迁成周（今洛阳）定在他即位那一年，东周由此开始。

detail.en: The Xinian bamboo slips held by Tsinghua University say that after King You died, nobles crowned a rival king, Yuchen, who reigned 21 years until Marquis Wen of Jin killed him. Jin then installed Ping, who moved east three years later. Scholars still debate how this fits the date 770 BCE.
detail.zh: 清华简《系年》记载，幽王死后，诸侯另立王子余臣为王（携惠王），在位21年后被晋文侯所杀；晋随后拥立平王，三年后才东迁成周。这一记载如何与前770年相合，学界仍有争论。

title.en: Duke Zhuang of Zheng 郑庄公

summary.en: Ruler of Zheng, r. 743–701 BCE. In 707 BCE his army defeated a coalition led by King Huan of Zhou at Xuge.
summary.zh: 郑国国君，前743—前701年在位。前707年，郑军在繻葛击败周桓王率领的联军。

detail.en: The Zuo Tradition says a Zheng officer, Zhu Dan, shot the king in the shoulder at Xuge. Duke Zhuang stopped the pursuit, and that night sent his minister Zhai Zu to ask after the king and his attendants.
detail.zh: 据《左传》，繻葛之战中郑将祝聃射中周桓王的肩膀。郑庄公下令不再追击，当夜又派祭足去慰问周王及其左右。

title.en: Duke Xiang of Qin 秦襄公

summary.en: Ruler of Qin, r. 777–766 BCE. Shiji says he escorted King Ping east with troops and was made a regional lord in return.
summary.zh: 秦国国君，前777—前766年在位。《史记》记载，他带兵护送周平王东迁，因此被封为诸侯。

detail.en: According to Shiji 5, King Ping granted Qin the land west of Mount Qi, on condition that Qin could drive out the Rong who held it. Duke Xiang died in 766 BCE while campaigning against the Rong near Qi.
detail.zh: 据《史记·秦本纪》，周平王把岐山以西的土地赐给秦，条件是秦能赶走占据那里的戎人。前766年，秦襄公在攻戎途中到达岐山时去世。

title.en: Duke Huan of Qi 齐桓公

summary.en: Ruler of Qi, r. 685–643 BCE. With Guan Zhong as chief minister he led covenant meetings of the states, claiming to protect the Zhou king; later writers called him the first hegemon.
summary.zh: 齐国国君，前685—前643年在位。他任用管仲为相，以尊奉周王为号召主持诸侯盟会，后世称他为春秋第一位霸主。

detail.en: Shiji 32 says that after he died in 643 BCE his sons fought over the succession, and his body lay on its bed unburied for 67 days, until worms crawled out of the door.
detail.zh: 据《史记·齐太公世家》，前643年齐桓公死后，几个儿子争夺君位，他的尸体在床上停放了67天无人收殓，尸虫一直爬到门外。

summary.en: Chief minister of Qi under Duke Huan, d. 645 BCE. Shiji credits him with making Qi rich and strong; many policies in the book Guanzi were written by later authors.
summary.zh: 齐桓公的国相，前645年卒。《史记》说他使齐国富强；以他命名的《管子》一书，有不少内容出自后人之手。

detail.en: Before Duke Huan took power, Guan Zhong served his rival brother, Prince Jiu, and, according to Shiji, shot Huan with an arrow that struck his belt hook. On Bao Shuya's advice, Huan made him chief minister anyway.
detail.zh: 齐桓公即位前，管仲辅佐与他争位的公子纠。据《史记》，管仲曾射中桓公的衣带钩。后来桓公听从鲍叔牙的建议，仍任命管仲为相。

title.en: King Xiang of Zhou 周襄王

summary.en: King of Zhou, r. 651–619 BCE. In his first year his envoy brought sacrificial meat to Duke Huan of Qi at the Kuiqiu covenant, a mark of royal favour.
summary.zh: 周王，前651—前619年在位。即位当年，他派使者到葵丘会盟，把祭肉赐给齐桓公，以示尊宠。

detail.en: In 636 BCE his half-brother, Prince Dai, drove him out of the capital. The Zuo Tradition says Duke Wen of Jin killed Prince Dai and restored the king the next year, and the king rewarded Jin with land.
detail.zh: 前636年，他的弟弟王子带把他赶出都城。据《左传》，次年晋文公杀死王子带，送周襄王回朝，周王把几处土地赐给了晋国。

title.en: Duke Xiang of Song 宋襄公

summary.en: Ruler of Song, r. 650–637 BCE. After Duke Huan of Qi died he tried to lead the states, but Chu defeated his army at the Hong River in 638 BCE.
summary.zh: 宋国国君，前650—前637年在位。齐桓公死后，他想主持诸侯，但前638年在泓水被楚军击败。

detail.en: The Zuo Tradition says he refused to attack the Chu army while it was crossing the river or before it had formed ranks. He was wounded in the thigh in the battle and died of the wound the following year.
detail.zh: 据《左传》，他不肯趁楚军渡河或尚未列阵时进攻。宋襄公在这场战斗中大腿受伤，次年因伤去世。

title.en: Chóng’ěr 重耳 · Duke Wen of Jin 晋文公

summary.en: Ruler of Jin as Duke Wen, r. 636–628 BCE. After 19 years in exile he returned to Jin, and in 632 BCE led the alliance that defeated Chu at Chengpu.
summary.zh: 晋国国君，即晋文公，前636—前628年在位。他流亡19年后回国即位，前632年率联军在城濮击败楚军。

detail.en: Shiji 39 says he was 62 when he returned with Qin's help. In exile he had promised the king of Chu that if their armies ever met, Jin would first pull back three days' march; the Zuo Tradition says he did so before Chengpu.
detail.zh: 据《史记·晋世家》，他在秦国帮助下回国时已62岁。流亡期间他曾对楚王说，若两国交兵，晋军先退避三舍；据《左传》，城濮之战前他兑现了这一承诺。

title.en: Duke Mu of Qin 秦穆公

summary.en: Ruler of Qin, r. 659–621 BCE. He helped Chong'er return to Jin. After Jin destroyed a Qin army at Xiao in 627 BCE, Qin turned west and, Shiji says, came to dominate the western Rong.
summary.zh: 秦国国君，前659—前621年在位。他曾帮助重耳回晋即位；前627年秦军在崤被晋军全歼后，秦转向西方，《史记》称其“遂霸西戎”。

detail.en: Shiji 5 says that when the three captured commanders were released and came home, Duke Mu met them outside the capital in white mourning clothes, wept, and blamed himself for ignoring advice against the raid.
detail.zh: 据《史记·秦本纪》，三位被俘的将领获释回国时，秦穆公穿着素服到郊外迎接，哭着说是自己不听百里傒、蹇叔的劝告，才让他们受辱。

title.en: King Zhuang of Chu 楚庄王

summary.en: King of Chu, r. 613–591 BCE. He extended Chu's power northward, and his army defeated Jin at Bi in 597 BCE.
summary.zh: 楚国国君，前613—前591年在位。他把楚国势力向北推进，前597年楚军在邲之战中击败晋军。

detail.en: The Zuo Tradition says that in 606 BCE, camped near the Zhou border, he asked the royal envoy Wangsun Man how large and heavy the Zhou tripods were. The envoy replied that the right to rule lay in virtue, not in the tripods.
detail.zh: 据《左传》，前606年楚庄王陈兵周境，向周王派来的王孙满打听九鼎的大小轻重。王孙满回答：“在德不在鼎。”

summary.en: A minister of Song, active mid-6th century BCE. In 546 BCE he arranged a meeting in the Song capital where Jin, Chu and their allies agreed to stop fighting each other.
summary.zh: 宋国大夫，活跃于前6世纪中叶。前546年，他促成晋、楚及其盟国在宋都会盟，约定彼此停战。

detail.en: The Zuo Tradition says that afterwards Xiang Xu asked for a reward and the duke granted him 60 towns, but the minister Zihan cut up the grant, arguing that no state could do away with weapons.
detail.zh: 据《左传》，弭兵之会后向戌请求封赏，宋平公赐给他60个邑，但大夫子罕把赏赐文书削毁，认为兵器不可能被废除。

summary.en: King of Wu, r. 514–496 BCE. With Wu Zixu among his advisers, he led the Wu army that captured the Chu capital Ying in 506 BCE.
summary.zh: 吴国国君，前514—前496年在位。他任用伍子胥等人，前506年率吴军攻入楚都郢。

detail.en: He took the throne after the assassin Zhuan Zhu stabbed King Liao with a blade hidden inside a fish served at a banquet. In 496 BCE he was wounded in the toe fighting Yue at Zuili and died of the wound.
detail.zh: 他是在刺客专诸把短剑藏在鱼腹中刺杀吴王僚后即位的。前496年，阖闾在檇李与越军交战时伤了脚趾，不久伤重而死。

summary.en: A Chu noble who fled to Wu after the king of Chu killed his father and elder brother in 522 BCE; he helped Wu capture the Chu capital Ying in 506 BCE. Died 484 BCE.
summary.zh: 楚国贵族，前522年楚平王杀其父兄后逃往吴国，前506年协助吴军攻入楚都郢。前484年卒。

detail.en: In 484 BCE King Fuchai, after quarrels over Yue and accusations by the minister Bo Pi, sent him a sword to kill himself. Shiji says his body was then put in a leather bag and thrown into the river.
detail.zh: 前484年，吴王夫差在与他争论对越政策、又听信太宰嚭的谗言后，赐剑令他自杀。据《史记》，他的尸体被装进皮袋，抛入江中。

summary.en: Dates unknown, late 6th century BCE. Shiji presents him as a strategist from Qi who served King Helü of Wu and wrote the 13 chapters of the Art of War; his historicity is debated.
summary.zh: 生卒年不详，约前6世纪末。《史记》说他是齐人，为吴王阖闾效力，著有兵法13篇；其人是否真实存在仍有争论。

detail.en: Shiji tells how he drilled 180 palace women for King Helü and executed the king's two favourite consorts who led them. The Zuo Tradition, the fullest record of this period, never mentions him, which is one reason scholars doubt the story.
detail.zh: 《史记》记载，孙武用180名宫女为阖闾演示练兵，并斩了领队的两位吴王宠姬。记述这一时期最详细的《左传》却从未提到他，这是学者怀疑此事的原因之一。

summary.en: King of Wu, r. 495–473 BCE. He defeated Yue in 494 BCE, campaigned north and met Jin at Huangchi in 482 BCE; Yue conquered Wu in 473 BCE.
summary.zh: 吴国国君，前495—前473年在位。前494年他击败越国，此后北上争霸，前482年与晋在黄池会盟；前473年吴被越所灭。

detail.en: When Yue besieged his capital in 473 BCE, Goujian offered to settle him at Yongdong with a hundred households. Shiji says he refused, covered his face because he could not face Wu Zixu, and killed himself.
detail.zh: 前473年越军围困吴都，勾践提出把他安置在甬东，给他百户人家。据《史记》，夫差拒绝了，说自己无颜见伍子胥，蒙住脸自杀。

summary.en: King of Yue, r. 496–465 BCE. Defeated by Wu in 494 BCE, he rebuilt Yue's strength and conquered Wu in 473 BCE.
summary.zh: 越国国君，前496—前465年在位。前494年被吴打败后重整国力，前473年灭吴。

detail.en: Shiji says that after his defeat he hung a gall bladder by his seat and tasted it before eating, to remind himself of his humiliation. The other half of the saying, sleeping on brushwood, is a later addition.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，战败后他把苦胆挂在座旁，吃饭前先尝一尝，提醒自己不忘耻辱。“卧薪”则是后世添加的说法。

summary.en: Dates unknown, early 5th century BCE. An adviser to King Goujian of Yue who, in Shiji's account, helped plan Yue's recovery and its conquest of Wu.
summary.zh: 生卒年不详，前5世纪初人。越王勾践的谋臣，据《史记》，曾参与谋划越国复兴和灭吴。

detail.en: According to Shiji, after Wu fell he left Yue and wrote to the minister Wen Zhong that once the birds are gone, the good bow is put away. Wen Zhong was later ordered to kill himself. Stories of Fan Li becoming a rich merchant are later tradition.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，灭吴后范蠡离开越国，写信给大夫文种说“蜚鸟尽，良弓藏”。后来文种被勾践赐死。范蠡经商致富的故事出自后世传说。

summary.en: 551–479 BCE. A teacher and minor official from Lu whose sayings, collected by his followers as the Analects, shaped later Chinese thought about government and family.
summary.zh: 前551—前479年，鲁国人，教师，也曾在鲁国任官。弟子编成的《论语》记录他的言论，深刻影响了后世关于治国与家庭的思想。

detail.en: Shiji 47 says he left Lu in about 497 BCE and spent some 14 years travelling between Wey, Chen, Cai and other states, at one point running out of food between Chen and Cai, before returning home. The order of these journeys is disputed.
detail.zh: 据《史记·孔子世家》，他约在前497年离开鲁国，在卫、陈、蔡等国之间奔走约14年，曾在陈、蔡之间断粮，最后回到鲁国。这些行程的先后次序仍有争议。

summary.en: Zhi Yao, d. 453 BCE. Head of the Zhi house, the strongest of the noble lineages ruling Jin; he led Han and Wei in flooding Zhao's city of Jinyang until they turned against him.
summary.zh: 即智瑶，前453年卒。智氏首领，当时在晋国执政的几大家族中势力最强。他率韩、魏两家引水灌赵氏的晋阳，最后韩、魏倒戈。

detail.en: Shiji says that after his defeat Zhao Xiangzi had his skull lacquered and used it as a drinking vessel. His retainer Yu Rang then tried more than once to kill Zhao Xiangzi in revenge.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，智伯败亡后，赵襄子把他的头骨漆成饮器。他的家臣豫让此后多次谋刺赵襄子，为他报仇。

summary.en: Head of the Zhao house in Jin, c. 475–425 BCE. Besieged at Jinyang, he won over Han and Wei, and in 453 BCE the three houses destroyed the Zhi house and divided its lands.
summary.zh: 晋国赵氏首领，约前475—前425年在位。被围于晋阳时，他争取到韩、魏两家倒戈，前453年三家联手灭智氏，瓜分其地。

detail.en: Shiji 43 says the floodwater rose to within three planks of the top of Jinyang's walls, and people hung their cooking pots up to keep them dry. Zhao Xiangzi sent Zhang Mengtan out secretly to persuade Han and Wei to change sides.
detail.zh: 据《史记·赵世家》，大水离晋阳城头只差三版，城中百姓只能把锅吊起来做饭。赵襄子暗中派张孟谈出城，说服韩、魏两家倒戈。

summary.en: Head of the Han 韩 house in Jin, mid-5th century BCE. He joined Zhi Bo's siege of Jinyang, then switched to Zhao's side; in 453 BCE Han, Zhao and Wei divided the Zhi lands.
summary.zh: 晋国韩氏首领，活跃于前5世纪中叶。他先随智伯围攻晋阳，后转投赵氏；前453年韩、赵、魏三家瓜分智氏土地。

detail.en: The Zhanguoce says that when Zhi Bo demanded territory, Han Kangzi handed over a town of 10,000 households rather than risk war. Zhao refused a similar demand, and the siege of Jinyang followed.
detail.zh: 据《战国策》，智伯向韩索地时，韩康子为避免开战，献出一座万户之邑。赵氏拒绝了同样的要求，随后便有晋阳之围。

summary.en: Head of the Wei 魏 house in Jin, mid-5th century BCE, and grandfather of Marquis Wen of Wei. He besieged Jinyang with Zhi Bo, then turned against Zhi in 453 BCE.
summary.zh: 晋国魏氏首领，活跃于前5世纪中叶，魏文侯的祖父。他曾随智伯围攻晋阳，前453年倒戈灭智氏。

detail.en: A speech recorded in Shiji 44 says Zhi Bo remarked that the Fen River could flood Anyi and the Jiang River could flood Pingyang, the chief towns of Wei and Han. Wei Huanzi nudged Han Kangzi with his elbow, and Han Kangzi trod on his foot.
detail.zh: 《史记·魏世家》所载一段说辞提到，智伯曾说汾水可以灌安邑，绛水可以灌平阳，这正是魏、韩两家的城邑。魏桓子用手肘碰了碰韩康子，韩康子踩了一下他的脚。

summary.en: Leader of the Tian (Chen) lineage of Qi, active c. 481 BCE. In 481 BCE he had Duke Jian killed, put Duke Ping on the throne, and ran the government as chancellor.
summary.zh: 齐国田氏（陈氏）首领，活跃于前481年前后。前481年，他杀死齐简公，拥立齐平公，以相国身份掌握朝政。

detail.en: Shiji 46 says the Tian house lent grain using a large measure and took repayment with a small one, winning popular support. Tian Chang later took the land east of Anping as his own fief, larger than the area the duke himself drew income from.
detail.zh: 据《史记·田敬仲完世家》，田氏用大斗借出粮食、小斗收回，以此收买人心。田常后来把安平以东的土地划为自己的封邑，比齐平公自己的食邑还大。

summary.en: Mo Di, c. 470–c. 391 BCE. A thinker who argued against wars of conquest and for impartial care for all; his followers became known for defending besieged cities.
summary.zh: 即墨翟，约前470—约前391年。反对攻伐、主张兼爱的思想家；他的门徒以帮助被围城邑守城著称。

detail.en: Shiji gives him only one line, calling him a Song official skilled in defence and frugal in spending, and adding that some say he lived at the same time as Confucius, others after him.
detail.zh: 《史记》只用一句话提到他，说他是宋国大夫，善于守御，主张节用；又说他或许与孔子同时，或许在孔子之后。

title.en: Marquis Wen of Wei 魏文侯

summary.en: Ruler of Wei 魏, r. 445–396 BCE. He employed Li Kui, Wu Qi and Ximen Bao, and in 403 BCE the Zhou king recognised Wei, Zhao and Han as states.
summary.zh: 魏国国君，前445—前396年在位。他任用李悝、吴起、西门豹等人；前403年，周王承认魏、赵、韩为诸侯。

detail.en: Shiji 44 says he studied the classics with Zixia, a disciple of Confucius, and whenever his carriage passed the home of the scholar Duan Ganmu he bowed from it in respect.
detail.zh: 据《史记·魏世家》，魏文侯曾随孔子弟子子夏学习经书；每次乘车经过隐士段干木的住处，都要扶轼致敬。

summary.en: An adviser to Marquis Wen of Wei, active late 5th century BCE, traditionally credited with reforms that raised farm output and with an early law code.
summary.zh: 魏文侯的谋臣，活跃于前5世纪末。传统上认为他推行了提高农业产量的改革，并编订了早期法典。

detail.en: Shiji credits him only with teaching Wei to use 'the full strength of the land', getting more grain from each field. The claim that he wrote the first law code, the Fajing, first appears in the Book of Jin, compiled more than 1,000 years later.
detail.zh: 《史记》只说他推行“尽地力之教”，即让每块田地多产粮食。说他编写最早的法典《法经》，最早见于一千多年后成书的《晋书》。

summary.en: c. 440–381 BCE. A commander and reformer from Wey 卫 who served Lu, then Wei 魏, then Chu, where King Dao backed his cuts to noble privileges.
summary.zh: 约前440—前381年，卫国人，军事家、改革者。先后在鲁、魏、楚任职，在楚国得到楚悼王支持，削减贵族特权。

detail.en: Shiji 65 says that when King Dao died in 381 BCE, nobles attacked Wu Qi at the funeral with arrows; he threw himself onto the king's body, and the arrows struck it too. The next king executed the members of more than 70 families for shooting the royal corpse.
detail.zh: 据《史记·孙子吴起列传》，前381年楚悼王死，贵族们在丧礼上用箭射杀吴起；吴起伏在悼王尸体上，箭也射中了王尸。新王即位后，因射中王尸而被灭族的有70多家。

title.en: King Dao of Chu 楚悼王

summary.en: King of Chu, r. 401–381 BCE. He made Wu Qi his chief minister and backed reforms that took office and income from distant royal relatives to support soldiers.
summary.zh: 楚国国君，前401—前381年在位。他任用吴起为令尹，推行改革，削去疏远王族的官位和俸禄，用来供养士兵。

detail.en: Shiji 65 says Wu Qi, with the king's backing, made the laws clear, dismissed unneeded officials and cut off distant royal clan members. After the king died, the nobles who had lost out killed Wu Qi at the funeral.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，吴起在楚悼王支持下明确法令、裁撤闲散官职、废除疏远公族的特权。悼王一死，利益受损的贵族就在丧礼上杀了吴起。

summary.en: d. 337 BCE. Chancellor of Han 韩 under Marquis Zhao for about 15 years, later grouped with the Legalists for his methods of checking officials' work against their posts.
summary.zh: 前337年卒。韩昭侯的国相，任职约15年。后人把他归入法家，因为他主张用“术”考核官吏是否名实相符。

detail.en: Shiji 63 says that during his years as chancellor Han was well governed and its army strong, and no state invaded Han while he lived.
detail.zh: 据《史记·老子韩非列传》，申不害为相期间，韩国内政修明，兵力强盛，在他有生之年没有国家侵犯韩国。

title.en: Duke Xiao of Qin 秦孝公

summary.en: Ruler of Qin, r. 361–338 BCE. He invited advisers from other states and backed Shang Yang's reforms from 356 BCE; Qin moved its capital to Xianyang in 350 BCE.
summary.zh: 秦国国君，前361—前338年在位。他招揽各国人才，从前356年起支持商鞅变法；前350年秦迁都咸阳。

detail.en: Shiji 5 says that in his first year he issued an order promising high office and a share of land to any guest or official who could find a way to make Qin strong. Shang Yang came to Qin in answer.
detail.zh: 据《史记·秦本纪》，秦孝公即位当年下令：宾客群臣中有能献出奇计使秦强大的，就授予高官，分给土地。商鞅正是应此令入秦的。

summary.en: c. 390–338 BCE. A noble from Wey 卫 who reorganised Qin from 356 BCE: households grouped for mutual responsibility, ranks earned by war merit, and counties run by appointed officials.
summary.zh: 约前390—前338年，卫国贵族。前356年起在秦变法：编户连坐，按军功授爵，设县由朝廷派官治理。

detail.en: After Duke Xiao died in 338 BCE, opponents accused Shang Yang of plotting rebellion. Shiji 68 says he fled, was caught, and the new ruler had his body torn apart by chariots and his whole family killed.
detail.zh: 前338年秦孝公死后，反对者告发商鞅谋反。据《史记·商君列传》，他出逃被捉，新君将他车裂示众，并杀尽了他的家人。

summary.en: Dates unknown, mid-4th century BCE. A strategist said to descend from Sun Wu; as adviser to the Qi commander Tian Ji, Shiji credits him with Qi's victories over Wei at Guiling and Maling.
summary.zh: 生卒年不详，前4世纪中叶人，相传是孙武的后代。作为齐将田忌的军师，《史记》把齐在桂陵、马陵两次战胜魏军归功于他。

detail.en: Shiji says his fellow student Pang Juan, jealous of his skill, had both his feet cut off; a Qi envoy smuggled him out of Wei. A text on his military methods, lost for about 2,000 years, was found in a tomb at Yinqueshan in 1972.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，他的同学庞涓嫉妒他的才能，对他施以膑刑，砍去双脚；后来齐国使者把他偷偷带出魏国。失传约2000年的《孙膑兵法》，1972年在银雀山汉墓中重新出土。

summary.en: d. 342 BCE (Shiji). A commander of Wei 魏 who, Shiji says, studied military arts alongside Sun Bin; Qi armies defeated him at Guiling in 353 BCE and at Maling.
summary.zh: 前342年卒（据《史记》）。魏国将领，《史记》说他曾与孙膑一同学习兵法。齐军先后在桂陵（前353年）和马陵击败他。

detail.en: Shiji 65 says that at Maling he found a stripped tree inscribed 'Pang Juan dies under this tree', was ambushed by Qi crossbowmen, and killed himself. The Yinqueshan slip text 'Capturing Pang Juan' instead says he was captured at Guiling.
detail.zh: 《史记》记载，马陵之战中庞涓看到一棵剥了皮的大树，上面写着“庞涓死于此树之下”，随即遭齐军弩手伏击，自杀而死。银雀山竹简《擒庞涓》则说他在桂陵就已被擒。

summary.en: A Qi commander, mid-4th century BCE. With Sun Bin as his adviser, Shiji says, he led Qi's armies against Wei at Guiling (353 BCE) and Maling (342 BCE).
summary.zh: 齐国将领，前4世纪中叶人。据《史记》，他以孙膑为军师，率齐军在桂陵（前353年）和马陵（前342年）与魏军作战。

detail.en: Shiji 65 tells how Sun Bin helped him win a horse-racing bet against the king of Qi: race his worst team against the king's best, and his best and middle teams against the king's middle and worst. Tian Ji lost one race, won two, and took the prize of 1,000 gold.
detail.zh: 《史记》记载，孙膑帮田忌与齐王赛马：用下等马对齐王的上等马，用上等马、中等马分别对齐王的中等马、下等马。田忌一负两胜，赢得千金。

summary.en: d. 309 BCE. A man from Wei 魏 who became Qin's chancellor and, in Shiji's account, persuaded the other states one by one to make separate terms with Qin.
summary.zh: 前309年卒，魏国人，后任秦相。据《史记》，他游说各国分别与秦交好，以拆散各国的联合。

detail.en: Shiji 70 says he told King Huai of Chu that Qin would give Chu 600 li of land if Chu broke with Qi; once Chu did so, he said he had promised only six. Chu attacked Qin and was defeated at Danyang in 312 BCE.
detail.zh: 据《史记·张仪列传》，张仪对楚怀王说，只要楚与齐绝交，秦就把商於之地600里送给楚。楚绝齐后，他却改口说只答应过6里。楚出兵攻秦，前312年在丹阳大败。

summary.en: d. c. 284 BCE. A persuader from Luoyang. Shiji makes him organiser of a six-state alliance against Qin around 333 BCE, but excavated letters place his career decades later.
summary.zh: 约前284年卒，洛阳人，纵横家。《史记》说他约在前333年联合六国抗秦，但出土书信显示他的主要活动要晚几十年。

detail.en: Letters found in a Mawangdui tomb in 1973, the Zhanguo zonghengjia shu, show him working for Yan at the court of Qi to weaken Qi. Most scholars now date his death to around 284 BCE, when Yan and its allies attacked Qi.
detail.zh: 1973年马王堆汉墓出土的帛书《战国纵横家书》显示，他曾为燕国在齐国活动，设法削弱齐国。现在多数学者认为他死于前284年前后，即燕与各国攻齐之时。

summary.en: Known as Xishou, active 330s–310s BCE. A man from Wei 魏 who served Qin and then Wei, and organised coalitions against Qin in opposition to Zhang Yi.
summary.zh: 号犀首，活跃于前330年代至前310年代。魏国人，先仕秦，后仕魏，组织各国联合抗秦，与张仪针锋相对。

detail.en: The Zhanguoce credits him with the 323 BCE arrangement in which the rulers of Wei, Han, Zhao, Yan and Zhongshan recognised one another as kings. In 318 BCE several states attacked Qin together and were driven back at the Hangu Pass.
detail.zh: 据《战国策》，前323年魏、韩、赵、燕、中山五国国君互相承认对方称王，是他促成的。前318年，几国联军攻秦，在函谷关被秦军击退。

title.en: King Huai of Chu 楚怀王

summary.en: King of Chu, r. 328–299 BCE. He broke with Qi on Zhang Yi's promise of land, then lost to Qin at Danyang in 312 BCE.
summary.zh: 楚国国君，前328—前299年在位。他听信张仪许地之言与齐绝交，前312年在丹阳败于秦军。

detail.en: In 299 BCE he went to meet King Zhaoxiang of Qin at the Wu Pass and was detained. Shiji 40 says he died in Qin in 296 BCE; when his body was returned, the people of Chu mourned him as if for their own family.
detail.zh: 前299年，他赴武关与秦昭襄王会面，被扣留在秦。据《史记·楚世家》，他前296年死于秦国；灵柩送回楚国时，楚人像哀悼亲人一样哀悼他。

summary.en: c. 340–c. 278 BCE (traditional dates). A Chu noble and official under King Huai, later exiled; the long poem Li Sao is attributed to him.
summary.zh: 约前340—约前278年（传统说法）。楚国贵族，曾在楚怀王朝中任职，后来被流放；长诗《离骚》相传是他的作品。

detail.en: Shiji 84 says he urged King Huai not to go to Qin, was later banished by King Qingxiang, and drowned himself in the Miluo River holding a stone. The year 278 BCE, when Qin took Ying, is a traditional date; Shiji gives no year.
detail.zh: 据《史记·屈原贾生列传》，他曾劝楚怀王不要去秦国，后来被楚顷襄王流放，抱石自沉汨罗江。前278年（秦攻破郢都那年）是传统说法，《史记》并没有写明年份。

title.en: King Wuling of Zhao 赵武灵王

summary.en: King of Zhao, r. 325–299 BCE. In 307 BCE he had Zhao's soldiers adopt the trousers and mounted archery of northern horse peoples, then expanded north and later conquered Zhongshan.
summary.zh: 赵国国君，前325—前299年在位。前307年，他推行“胡服骑射”，让赵军改穿北方游牧人群的服装、练习骑马射箭，随后向北扩张，后来又灭了中山。

detail.en: In 299 BCE he handed the throne to his son and took the title Zhufu. Shiji 43 says that in 295 BCE, after a failed revolt by his elder son, he was trapped in the Shaqiu palace for more than three months and starved to death.
detail.zh: 前299年他把王位传给儿子，自称“主父”。据《史记·赵世家》，前295年长子叛乱失败后，他被困在沙丘宫中三个多月，最后饿死。

summary.en: d. 265 BCE. A woman from Chu who became mother of King Zhaoxiang of Qin; after 306 BCE she and her brother Wei Ran directed Qin's government for decades.
summary.zh: 前265年卒。楚国人，秦昭襄王的母亲。前306年以后，她与弟弟魏冉主持秦国朝政达数十年。

detail.en: Shiji says she lured the king of the Yiqu, a people on Qin's northern frontier, to the Ganquan palace and had him killed; Qin then attacked and broke up Yiqu. The Hou Hanshu dates this to 272 BCE.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，她把秦国北边义渠人的首领诱到甘泉宫杀死，秦随即出兵攻破义渠。《后汉书》把此事系于前272年。

summary.en: A commander from Wei 魏 who served King Zhao of Yan; in 284 BCE he led an allied army that took Qi's capital Linzi.
summary.zh: 魏国人，后为燕昭王效力。前284年，他统率各国联军攻破齐都临淄。

detail.en: Shiji 80 says he took more than 70 Qi cities in five years; only Ju and Jimo held out. When the new king of Yan replaced him in 279 BCE, he fled to Zhao, fearing he would be executed.
detail.zh: 据《史记·乐毅列传》，他用五年时间攻下齐国70多座城，只剩莒和即墨未下。前279年燕惠王派人替换他，乐毅担心被杀，逃往赵国。

summary.en: Meng Ke, c. 372–c. 289 BCE. A teacher from Zou who followed Confucius's teachings and advised kings of Wei 魏 and Qi, arguing that rulers must keep the people's support.
summary.zh: 即孟轲，约前372—约前289年，邹国人。他继承孔子学说，曾游说魏、齐等国君主，主张君主必须得到民心。

detail.en: The Mengzi records that after Qi occupied Yan in 314 BCE, Mencius told King Xuan of Qi that Qi troops were killing fathers and brothers, binding sons and destroying ancestral temples, and urged him to return captives and withdraw.
detail.zh: 据《孟子·梁惠王下》，前314年齐军占领燕国后，孟子对齐宣王说，齐军杀害燕人的父兄，捆走他们的子弟，毁坏他们的宗庙，劝齐王放回俘虏、撤军。

summary.en: d. 257 BCE. A Qin commander whose victories at Yique (293 BCE), Ying (278 BCE) and Changping (260 BCE) killed or captured hundreds of thousands of soldiers, according to Shiji.
summary.zh: 前257年卒。秦国将领，据《史记》，他在伊阙（前293年）、郢（前278年）、长平（前260年）等战役中斩杀、俘虏对方士兵数十万人。

detail.en: In 257 BCE the king of Qin ordered him to kill himself. Shiji 73 says he first reflected that he deserved death, because at Changping several hundred thousand Zhao soldiers had surrendered and he had tricked them and buried them all.
detail.zh: 前257年，秦王命他自杀。据《史记·白起王翦列传》，他临死前说，长平之战赵军投降的有几十万人，自己用欺骗的手段把他们全部坑杀，这就足以该死了。

summary.en: A Zhao commander, active c. 283–245 BCE. At Changping he held fortified lines and avoided battle; in 260 BCE the Zhao king replaced him with Zhao Kuo after Qin agents spread rumours.
summary.zh: 赵国将领，活跃于约前283—前245年。长平之战中他坚守营垒、不与秦军决战；前260年秦人散布流言，赵王改派赵括取代他。

detail.en: Shiji 81 tells how he once went to Lin Xiangru's house bare-backed, carrying thorny sticks, to apologise for slighting him. In old age he left Zhao for Wei and then Chu, and died at Shouchun.
detail.zh: 据《史记·廉颇蔺相如列传》，他曾袒露上身、背着荆条到蔺相如门前请罪。晚年他离开赵国，先到魏国，后到楚国，死于寿春。

summary.en: d. 260 BCE. Son of the Zhao general Zhao She; sent to replace Lian Po at Changping, he attacked the Qin lines and his army was surrounded.
summary.zh: 前260年卒。赵国名将赵奢之子。他被派到长平接替廉颇，主动进攻秦军，结果赵军被包围。

detail.en: Shiji says that after 46 days surrounded without food, he led picked troops in an attempt to break out and was shot dead; the rest of the Zhao army then surrendered.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，赵军被围断粮46天后，赵括亲率精兵突围，被秦军射杀，其余赵军随即投降。

summary.en: Governor of Shangdang for Han 韩, active 262–260 BCE. When Qin cut Shangdang off from Han, he offered the district to Zhao; Zhao accepted, and the Changping war followed.
summary.zh: 韩国上党郡守，活跃于前262—前260年。秦军切断上党与韩国本土的联系后，他把上党献给赵国；赵国接受，随后爆发长平之战。

detail.en: Shiji 43 records his message to Zhao: Han could not hold Shangdang, its officials and people preferred Zhao to Qin, and its 17 walled towns were offered to the king of Zhao.
detail.zh: 据《史记·赵世家》，冯亭派人对赵王说：韩国守不住上党，当地官民宁愿归赵也不愿归秦，愿把上党17座城邑献给赵国。

summary.en: d. c. 255 BCE. A man from Wei 魏 who became Qin's chancellor in 266 BCE; Shiji credits him with the policy of befriending distant states and attacking nearby ones.
summary.zh: 约前255年卒，魏国人，前266年任秦相。《史记》把“远交近攻”的方略归于他。

detail.en: Shiji says that in Wei, accused of selling secrets to Qi, he was beaten until his ribs broke, rolled in a reed mat and left in a privy. He escaped to Qin under a false name.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，他在魏国被怀疑向齐国泄密，被打断肋骨，用草席卷起扔进厕所。后来他化名张禄逃到秦国。

summary.en: Zhao Sheng, d. 251 BCE. A Zhao prince and chancellor known for his thousands of retainers; during the Qin siege of Handan (258–257 BCE) he sought help from Chu and Wei.
summary.zh: 即赵胜，前251年卒。赵国公子，曾任相国，门下食客数千人。前258—前257年秦围邯郸时，他向楚、魏求援。

detail.en: Shiji 76 says he took 20 retainers to Chu to ask for an alliance. When talks stalled, Mao Sui, who had volunteered himself, climbed the steps with his hand on his sword and pressed the king of Chu until he agreed.
detail.zh: 据《史记·平原君虞卿列传》，他带20名门客去楚国求援。谈判没有结果时，自荐随行的毛遂按剑登阶，逼楚王当场答应结盟。

summary.en: Wei Wuji, d. 243 BCE. A half-brother of King Anxi of Wei 魏; in 257 BCE he took command of a Wei army with a stolen tally and relieved the Qin siege of Handan.
summary.zh: 即魏无忌，前243年卒。魏安釐王的异母弟。前257年他凭盗来的兵符夺得魏军指挥权，解了秦军对邯郸的包围。

detail.en: Shiji 77 says the commander Jin Bi doubted the tally, so Xinling Jun's follower Zhu Hai killed him with a 40-jin iron mallet hidden in his sleeve. In 247 BCE Xinling Jun led five states' armies that pushed Qin back to the Hangu Pass.
detail.zh: 据《史记·魏公子列传》，魏将晋鄙对兵符起疑，信陵君的门客朱亥便用藏在袖中的40斤铁椎将他打死。前247年，信陵君率五国联军把秦军打退到函谷关。

summary.en: A favoured consort of King Anxi of Wei 魏, active 257 BCE. Shiji says she took the tiger tally from the king's bedchamber so that Xinling Jun could take command of the army.
summary.zh: 魏安釐王的宠姬，活跃于前257年。据《史记》，她从魏王卧室中偷出虎符，让信陵君得以接管魏军。

detail.en: Shiji 77 explains why she helped: her father had been murdered, and for three years no one could find the killer until a retainer of Xinling Jun beheaded him and presented the head to her.
detail.zh: 《史记·魏公子列传》说明了她相助的原因：她的父亲被人杀害，三年都找不到凶手，后来信陵君派门客斩下仇人的头，送到她面前。

summary.en: Huang Xie, d. 238 BCE. Chancellor of Chu from 262 BCE; in 257 BCE he led Chu troops to help relieve the Qin siege of Handan.
summary.zh: 即黄歇，前238年卒。前262年起任楚国令尹；前257年率楚军参与救援被秦军围困的邯郸。

detail.en: He had stayed in Qin as companion to the Chu crown prince and helped him escape home; the prince became King Kaolie and made him chancellor. Shiji says that days after the king's death in 238 BCE, Li Yuan's men ambushed and killed him at a palace gate.
detail.zh: 他曾陪同楚太子在秦国做人质，并帮太子逃回楚国；太子即位为楚考烈王后，任他为令尹。据《史记》，前238年考烈王去世后不久，他在宫门被李园埋伏的刺客杀死。

title.en: King Zhaoxiang of Qin 秦昭襄王

summary.en: King of Qin, r. 306–251 BCE. During his 56-year reign Qin took Chu's capital Ying (278 BCE) and won at Changping (260 BCE), but failed to take Handan (257 BCE).
summary.zh: 秦国国君，前306—前251年在位。在他在位的56年间，秦攻破楚都郢（前278年），赢得长平之战（前260年），但没能攻下邯郸（前257年）。

detail.en: Shiji 5 says that in 255 BCE the people of Zhou fled east and the nine Zhou ritual tripods were taken to Qin.
detail.zh: 据《史记·秦本纪》，前255年周的百姓向东逃散，周王室的九鼎被运入秦国。

summary.en: A Qi official, active 284–279 BCE. Defending Jimo after Yan's invasion, he broke the siege in 279 BCE and Qi recovered its lost cities.
summary.zh: 齐国人，活跃于前284—前279年。燕军攻齐后，他坚守即墨，前279年突围反攻，齐国收复了失地。

detail.en: Shiji 82 says he gathered more than 1,000 oxen, tied blades to their horns and fat-soaked reeds to their tails, and set them loose at night against the Yan camp. The Yan commander Qi Jie was killed, and Qi recovered more than 70 cities.
detail.zh: 据《史记·田单列传》，他集中1000多头牛，在牛角上绑上利刃，在牛尾上绑上浸过油脂的芦苇，夜里点火，把牛群赶向燕军营地。燕将骑劫被杀，齐国收复70多座城。

title.en: King Nan of Zhou 周赧王

summary.en: King of Zhou, r. 314–256 BCE. The last reigning Zhou king; by his time the court controlled only a few towns around Luoyang, split between two Zhou lords.
summary.zh: 周王，前314—前256年在位，最后一位周天子。这时周王室只剩洛阳附近的几座城邑，还分属东、西两个周君。

detail.en: Shiji 4 says that in 256 BCE, after the Lord of Western Zhou surrendered 36 towns and 30,000 people to Qin, King Nan died the same year. The separate domain of the Lord of Eastern Zhou lasted until Qin took it in 249 BCE.
detail.zh: 据《史记·周本纪》，前256年西周君向秦献出36座城邑和3万人口，同年周赧王去世。东周君的领地一直延续到前249年才被秦攻取。

title.en: Yíng Zhèng 嬴政 · First Emperor of Qin

summary.en: 259–210 BCE. King of Qin from 247 BCE, ruling in person from 238 BCE; his armies conquered the other six states by 221 BCE, when he took the new title huangdi, 'emperor'.
summary.zh: 前259—前210年。前247年即位为秦王，前238年开始亲政；到前221年，秦军攻灭其余六国，他改用新称号“皇帝”。

detail.en: Shiji 6 says that in 221 BCE he divided the conquered lands into 36 commanderies, had weapons collected and melted into 12 giant bronze figures, and made laws, weights, measures and axle widths the same everywhere.
detail.zh: 据《史记·秦始皇本纪》，前221年他把天下分为36郡，收缴兵器熔铸成12个铜人，并统一法令、度量衡和车轨宽度。

summary.en: d. 235 BCE. A merchant who backed the Qin prince Zichu; when Zichu became king, Lü became chancellor, and he held power in the early years of Ying Zheng's reign.
summary.zh: 前235年卒。商人出身，曾扶助在外做人质的秦公子子楚。子楚即位后，他任相国，嬴政即位初年仍掌握大权。

detail.en: Shiji 85 says he displayed his book, the Lüshi chunqiu, at the Xianyang market gate and offered 1,000 gold to anyone who could add or remove a single word. Dismissed and ordered to move to Shu, he drank poison in 235 BCE.
detail.zh: 据《史记·吕不韦列传》，他把《吕氏春秋》公布在咸阳城门，宣称谁能增删一字就赏千金。后来他被罢免，又被命令迁往蜀地，前235年饮毒酒自杀。

summary.en: c. 280–208 BCE. A man from Shangcai in Chu who became Qin's chancellor; he argued against restoring hereditary kingdoms and in 213 BCE proposed burning books.
summary.zh: 约前280—前208年，楚国上蔡人，后任秦国丞相。他反对重新分封诸侯，前213年提出焚书的建议。

detail.en: Shiji 87 says that in 208 BCE, after Zhao Gao accused him of treason, he was cut in two at the waist in the Xianyang market, and his relatives to the third degree were killed.
detail.zh: 据《史记·李斯列传》，前208年他被赵高诬告谋反，在咸阳街市被腰斩，并被夷灭三族。

summary.en: c. 280–233 BCE. A prince of Han 韩 whose essays argued that rulers should govern through clear laws, methods of control and authority. Sent to Qin in 233 BCE, he died there in prison.
summary.zh: 约前280—前233年，韩国公子。他在文章中主张君主依靠法、术、势来治国。前233年出使秦国，死于秦国狱中。

detail.en: Shiji 63 says he stammered and could not argue well, but wrote brilliantly. In Qin, Li Si and Yao Jia accused him, and Li Si sent him poison; the king of Qin later regretted it and sent a pardon, but Han Fei was already dead.
detail.zh: 据《史记·老子韩非列传》，韩非口吃，不善言谈，却擅长著书。到秦国后，李斯、姚贾诬陷他，李斯派人送去毒药；秦王后来后悔，派人赦免，但韩非已经死了。

summary.en: d. 229 BCE. A Zhao commander who guarded the northern frontier against the Xiongnu and defeated Qin armies in 233–232 BCE; Zhao's court had him executed in 229 BCE.
summary.zh: 前229年卒。赵国将领，长期在北方边境防御匈奴，前233—前232年又击败秦军；前229年被赵国朝廷处死。

detail.en: Shiji 81 says Qin paid large sums to Guo Kai, a favourite of the Zhao king, to claim that Li Mu was planning rebellion. When Li Mu refused to hand over command, he was arrested and beheaded; three months later Qin took Handan.
detail.zh: 据《史记·廉颇蔺相如列传》，秦国用重金收买赵王宠臣郭开，让他诬告李牧谋反。李牧拒绝交出兵权，被捕后斩首；三个月后秦军攻破邯郸。

summary.en: A Qin commander from Pinyang, active 236–223 BCE. His armies took Zhao's capital Handan (228 BCE) and, with 600,000 men by Shiji's count, conquered Chu (224–223 BCE).
summary.zh: 秦国将领，频阳人，活跃于前236—前223年。他率军攻破赵都邯郸（前228年）；据《史记》，又率60万大军灭楚（前224—前223年）。

detail.en: Shiji 73 says that before marching on Chu he repeatedly asked the king for fields and houses for his family, telling a friend this would reassure the king that he wanted nothing more than wealth.
detail.zh: 据《史记·白起王翦列传》，出兵攻楚前，他一再向秦王讨要良田美宅，对旁人解释说，这样秦王才会相信他只求富贵，别无他图。

summary.en: Son of Wang Jian. He flooded Wei's capital Daliang in 225 BCE, captured the kings of Yan and Dai in 222 BCE, and received Qi's surrender in 221 BCE.
summary.zh: 王翦之子。前225年他引水灌魏都大梁，前222年俘虏燕王和代王，前221年接受齐国投降。

detail.en: Shiji says his army diverted water from the Yellow River canal into Daliang; after three months the walls gave way and King Jia of Wei surrendered.
detail.zh: 据《史记》，王贲引黄河的渠水灌大梁，三个月后城墙崩坏，魏王假请降。

summary.en: A Qin commander, active 226–221 BCE. He pursued Yan's Crown Prince Dan in 226 BCE, and in about 225 BCE led 200,000 men against Chu and was defeated; the date is inferred from Shiji.
summary.zh: 秦国将领，活跃于前226—前221年。前226年他追击燕太子丹；约前225年率20万人攻楚，被楚军打败（年份由《史记》推定）。

detail.en: Shiji 73 says Wang Jian had asked for 600,000 men, but the king chose Li Xin's plan. Chu troops pursued his army for three days and nights, broke into two of its camps and killed seven commanders.
detail.zh: 据《史记·白起王翦列传》，王翦认为攻楚需要60万人，秦王却采纳了李信的方案。楚军尾随秦军三天三夜，攻破两座营垒，杀死7名都尉。

summary.en: d. 224 or 223 BCE. A Chu commander who fought Wang Jian's invasion of Chu, and grandfather of Xiang Yu, who later led the rising against Qin.
summary.zh: 前224或前223年卒。楚国将领，曾抵抗王翦率领的秦军；他的孙子项羽后来成为反秦的领袖。

detail.en: Shiji chapters disagree on his end. Shiji 6 says he made Lord Changping king of Chu and killed himself after defeat in 223 BCE; Shiji 73 says Wang Jian's army killed him in battle before the Chu king was captured.
detail.zh: 《史记》各篇对他的结局说法不一。《秦始皇本纪》说他拥立昌平君为楚王，前223年兵败后自杀；《白起王翦列传》则说他在楚王被俘之前就已被王翦的军队所杀。

summary.en: d. 227 BCE. A swordsman from Wey 卫 sent by Crown Prince Dan of Yan to kill the king of Qin; he failed and was killed at the Qin court.
summary.zh: 前227年卒，卫国人，剑客。燕太子丹派他刺杀秦王，行刺失败，被杀死在秦廷上。

detail.en: Shiji 86 says he brought the head of the Qin exile Fan Yuqi and a map of Yan's Dukang district with a poisoned dagger rolled inside. When the map was unrolled he seized the king's sleeve and stabbed, but missed, and was cut down. The farewell song at the Yi River is a literary scene.
detail.zh: 据《史记·刺客列传》，他带着秦国逃将樊於期的首级和燕国督亢地图，毒匕首卷在图中。地图展开到尽头，他抓住秦王的衣袖刺去，没有刺中，随即被杀。易水送别时的歌，是带有文学色彩的场景。

title.en: Crown Prince Dan of Yan 燕太子丹

summary.en: d. 226 BCE. Son of King Xi of Yan; once a hostage in Qin, he escaped home and in 227 BCE sent Jing Ke to assassinate the king of Qin.
summary.zh: 前226年卒。燕王喜之子。他曾在秦国做人质，后逃回燕国；前227年派荆轲刺杀秦王。

detail.en: After the attempt failed, Qin attacked and took the Yan capital Ji in 226 BCE. Shiji says King Xi, fleeing to Liaodong, had Dan killed and sent his head to Qin, hoping to stop the attack.
detail.zh: 行刺失败后，秦军进攻燕国，前226年攻破燕都蓟城。据《史记》，燕王喜逃到辽东，下令杀死太子丹，把他的头献给秦国，希望秦军停止进攻。

title.en: King Jian of Qi 齐王建

summary.en: King of Qi, r. 264–221 BCE. Qi stayed out of the wars against Qin for some 40 years; in 221 BCE he surrendered to Wang Ben without a battle.
summary.zh: 齐国末代国君，前264—前221年在位。齐国有40多年没有参与抗秦战争；前221年，他不战而降于王贲。

detail.en: Shiji 46 says his chancellor Hou Sheng took bribes from Qin and urged him not to join the other states. After his surrender he was moved to Gong, and Qi people sang a song blaming those advisers; the Zhanguoce says he starved to death there.
detail.zh: 据《史记·田敬仲完世家》，齐相后胜收受秦国贿金，劝齐王不要与各国联合。齐王建投降后被迁到共地，齐人编歌怨他听信奸臣；《战国策》说他最后在那里饿死。

summary.en: d. 210 BCE. A Qin commander who from 215 BCE led 300,000 troops against the Xiongnu and directed the building of walls along the northern frontier.
summary.zh: 前210年卒。秦国将领，从前215年起率30万大军北击匈奴，主持修筑北方边境的长城。

detail.en: Ordered to die after the First Emperor's death, he wondered, Shiji 88 says, whether his crime was cutting through the 'veins of the earth' with more than 10,000 li of walls, then took poison. Sima Qian commented that his real fault was working the people too hard.
detail.zh: 始皇死后，他被下令自杀。据《史记·蒙恬列传》，他临死前想到，自己修筑一万多里城墙，难免截断了地脉，这或许就是罪过，随后服毒而死。司马迁则评论说，他的过错在于不惜民力。

summary.en: d. 207 BCE. A Qin palace official who, with Li Si, hid the First Emperor's death in 210 BCE and forged orders that made Huhai emperor and forced Fusu to die.
summary.zh: 前207年卒。秦朝宫中官员。前210年他与李斯隐瞒秦始皇死讯，伪造诏书，立胡亥为帝，逼扶苏自杀。

detail.en: Shiji 6 says he presented a deer to the Second Emperor and called it a horse, then secretly punished the officials who said it was a deer. In 207 BCE he forced the Second Emperor to kill himself, and was then killed by Ziying.
detail.zh: 据《史记·秦始皇本纪》，他把一头鹿献给秦二世，说是马，事后暗中处置了说是鹿的大臣。前207年他逼秦二世自杀，随后被子婴所杀。

summary.en: d. 210 BCE. Eldest son of the First Emperor, sent to Meng Tian's northern army after objecting to his father's punishment of scholars; a forged edict ordered him to kill himself.
summary.zh: 前210年卒。秦始皇长子，因劝谏父亲不要严惩儒生，被派到北方蒙恬军中监军。后来一道伪造的诏书命他自杀。

detail.en: Shiji 87 says Meng Tian urged him to ask the court to confirm the order, but Fusu replied that when a father orders his son to die, there is nothing to ask, and killed himself.
detail.zh: 据《史记·李斯列传》，蒙恬劝他先向朝廷核实诏令，扶苏说：“父而赐子死，尚安复请！”随即自杀。

summary.en: d. 208 BCE. A hired farm labourer from Yangcheng who in 209 BCE led conscripts in a rising at Dazexiang and declared himself king at Chen; his own driver killed him six months later.
summary.zh: 前208年卒，阳城人，曾受雇为人耕田。前209年他在大泽乡率戍卒起事，在陈称王；六个月后被自己的车夫杀死。

detail.en: Shiji 48 says the conscripts rose because rain had made them late, and under Qin law lateness meant death. Qin legal texts excavated at Shuihudi set only reprimands and fines for lateness in labour service; scholars debate whether stricter rules applied to garrison duty.
detail.zh: 据《史记·陈涉世家》，戍卒因大雨误了期限，按秦法误期当斩，于是起事。睡虎地出土的秦律对徭役误期只规定训斥和罚款；戍边是否另有更重的规定，学界仍有讨论。

summary.en: d. 208 BCE. Co-leader with Chen Sheng of the Dazexiang rising of 209 BCE; he later led the siege of Xingyang and was killed by one of his own officers.
summary.zh: 前208年卒。前209年与陈胜一同领导大泽乡起事，后来率军围攻荥阳，被部将杀死。

detail.en: Shiji 48 says the two leaders hid a cloth reading 'Chen Sheng will be king' inside a fish for the conscripts to find, and Wu Guang imitated a fox's cry at night by a shrine, calling 'Great Chu will rise'.
detail.zh: 据《史记·陈涉世家》，两人把写着“陈胜王”的帛书塞进鱼腹，让戍卒发现；吴广又在夜里躲在祠堂旁学狐狸叫，喊“大楚兴，陈胜王”。

summary.en: d. 206 BCE. The last ruler of Qin, who had Zhao Gao killed and reigned as king, not emperor, for 46 days before surrendering to Liu Bang.
summary.zh: 前206年卒。秦的最后一位君主。他设计杀了赵高，只称秦王而不称皇帝，在位46天后向刘邦投降。

detail.en: Shiji 6 says he surrendered at Zhidao in a white carriage with a cord around his neck. When Xiang Yu reached Xianyang more than a month later, he killed Ziying and the Qin royal clan and burned the palaces. Shiji chapters disagree on how Ziying was related to the First Emperor.
detail.zh: 据《史记·秦始皇本纪》，他颈系丝带，乘白马素车，在轵道旁投降。一个多月后项羽进入咸阳，杀死子婴和秦宗室，焚烧宫室。《史记》各篇对子婴与始皇的亲属关系说法不一。

summary.en: Xun Kuang, c. 313–c. 238 BCE. A thinker from Zhao who argued that people become good through learning and ritual, and who taught both Han Fei and Li Si.
summary.zh: 即荀况，约前313—约前238年，赵国人。他认为人要通过学习和礼义才能变好，韩非和李斯都是他的学生。

detail.en: Shiji 74 says he three times served as the senior scholar at Qi's Jixia academy, then became magistrate of Lanling in Chu under Lord Chunshen, and stayed at Lanling after Chunshen's death in 238 BCE.
detail.zh: 据《史记·孟子荀卿列传》，他曾三次在齐国稷下学宫担任祭酒，后来在春申君手下任楚国兰陵令，春申君死后仍留居兰陵。

summary.en: Invaded by Qi and Wei, Zhao breaks the Yellow River dykes and floods their armies, which withdraw.
summary.zh: 齐、魏攻赵，赵国掘开黄河堤防，放水淹敌，齐魏军队撤走。

detail.en: The Shiji records it in a few words: 'we broke the river and flooded them, and the troops left.' It does not say where the dykes were cut or who drowned. The point marks the old course of the Yellow River between Zhao and Wei.
detail.zh: 《赵世家》只有寥寥几字：“齐、魏伐我，我决河水灌之，兵去。”史书没有说堤防在哪里掘开，也没有说淹死了谁。图上的点标在赵、魏之间的古黄河河道附近。

summary.en: Zhao breaks the Yellow River dykes again, this time to attack Wei; the floods spread to the Zhang River.
summary.zh: 赵国再次掘开黄河堤防攻魏，大水泛滥，漳水也漫出河道。

detail.en: The Shiji says: 'broke the river to attack Wei; great floods, the Zhang overflowed.' As in 332 BCE, it gives no place and no count of the people affected.
detail.zh: 《赵世家》记载：“决河水，伐魏氏。大潦，漳水出。”和前332年一样，没有记地点，也没有记受灾的人数。
